# US-03 — Summary and payment · Spec

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Story | [story.md](story.md) (verbatim, not edited) |
| Status | Approved |
| Version | 0.1 |
| Author | spec-writer subagent (Claude Opus 5.5) |
| Approved by | v0.1: Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21 (HC1 round 1) |
| Related ADRs | [ADR-0001](../../adr/0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) (`terms` per country with a required `country` relation; `/:country/resumen`; implementation note: summary route and `summaryStepGuard` registered by US-02), [ADR-0002](../../adr/0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) as amended by [ADR-0005](../../adr/0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) (public `find` on terms, proxy `/api/terms`, published-only reads, e2e token scope), [ADR-0003](../../adr/0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) (clear on successful payment, keep on rejected payment, terms and payment data never stored), [ADR-0006](../../adr/0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) (typed attributes, `localeTag`), [ADR-0007](../../adr/0007-simulated-price-rule.md) (`calculateFinalPrice` reused). **Needed:** simulated payment design (US-03-Q-01); terms rich-text format and safe rendering (US-03-Q-02). See §10. |

Sources cited in this spec:

- **Story**: [story.md](story.md).
- **Assessment**: requirements quoted verbatim from the assessment PDF by the orchestrator (not in
  the repository).
- **US-01**: [specs/US-01/spec.md](../US-01/spec.md) v0.5 (Approved): the typed step 1 output and
  reserved keys (§7.3), code-owned copy (§8.1), seed values ([seed-fields.md](../US-01/seed-fields.md)).
- **US-02**: [specs/US-02/spec.md](../US-02/spec.md) v0.1 (Approved): the stored `plan: { key }`,
  the offered plans, price display and formatting (BR-03), what it handed to US-03 (§7.4), and the
  summary route and guard (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15).
- **ADR-0001..0007**: accepted ADRs (precedence level 2), with the implementation notes in
  [adr/README.md](../../adr/README.md).
- **Reviews** of US-01 (R1..R4) and US-02 (R1, R2): lessons for a new content type (published-only
  router config, anonymous variants in the draft checks, no bespoke backend code where the schema
  suffices) and the `review-checklist` items on rich text, masking and the disabled pay button.

## 1. Summary

Step 3 of the quote wizard. After choosing a plan, a person in Colombia or Chile sees a summary
of their data, their vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price; the document number
is partially masked. From the summary they can go back to edit their data or change the plan.
They read the terms and conditions configured in Strapi for their country, accept them, and pay.
Payment is simulated: no real gateway, no card data. While the simulated payment runs, the pay
button is locked so it cannot be submitted twice. On success the stored quote is cleared and a
confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown; on rejection a clear message is shown and the
person can try again with all their information intact. The same build serves both countries.

## 2. Scope

**In scope**

- The summary page attached to the existing route `/:country/resumen`, behind the existing
  `summaryStepGuard`, without changing the address or the guard (ADR-0001 implementation note).
- Showing step 1 values with their Strapi labels, the chosen plan and its final price (reusing
  `calculateFinalPrice`, ADR-0007, and the US-02 money formatter); masking the document number.
- "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" back to steps 1 and 2.
- A per-country terms content type in Strapi (ADR-0001), its seed for CO and CL
  ([seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md)), public read access (ADR-0002 anticipates `find` and
  `/api/terms`), safe rendering of its formatted text.
- Accepting the terms, the pay button state, the simulated payment (success and rejection), double
  submit prevention, the simulated quote number, the confirmation, and clearing the wizard state on
  success (ADR-0003).
- Loading, error, retry and "not available" states of the terms.
- Keyboard-only use, accessible names, focus management, mobile and desktop layouts.
- Completing the assessment's full-flow e2e `frontend/e2e/us-01-03-full-flow-co.spec.ts` with the
  summary, terms, payment and confirmation.

**Out of scope**

- Real payment gateways, card or bank data of any kind, real charges ("Payment is simulated: a
  button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment
  gateways or use real card data.", Assessment).
- Issuing a policy, sending e-mails, PDFs or receipts, storing quotes on a server ("a database is
  not required", Assessment).
- Versioning of the terms or recording which version was accepted (US-03-Q-12).
- Requiring the person to scroll to the end of the terms before accepting (US-03-Q-12).
- Editing data inline on the summary; returning from step 1 straight to the summary (US-03-Q-11).
- Masking any value other than the document number; reformatting typed values (plates, RUT).
- Payment instalments, discounts, taxes.

## 3. Glossary

Terms defined in the US-01 and US-02 glossaries (country context, published, wizard state, typed
step 1 output, reserved key, offered plan, plan key, final price, today, editor) keep their meaning.

| Term | Meaning in this project |
|---|---|
| Summary | Step 3 of the wizard at `/:country/resumen`: the person's data, the chosen plan, the terms and the pay action. |
| Terms | The terms and conditions of one country: one published Strapi document of the terms content type (§7.1). |
| Accepting the terms | Checking the code-owned checkbox "Acepto los términos y condiciones". Held in the page's memory only (US-03-Q-10). |
| Masked document number | The display form of the reserved `documentNumber` value defined in BR-02. Computed at display time; never stored (ADR-0003). |
| Simulated payment | A front-end-only stand-in for a payment gateway, with a deterministic outcome and no card data (BR-08, US-03-Q-01). |
| Payment attempt | One activation of "Pagar" that the simulated payment accepts, from the start of processing to its outcome. |
| Quote number | The simulated identifier shown on the confirmation (US-03-Q-07). Not stored and not sent anywhere. |
| Confirmation | What the person sees after a successful payment (US-03-Q-06, US-03-Q-13). |

## 4. Business rules

| ID | Original (source) | Refined (precise, testable) | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|
| US-03-BR-01 | Story: "The summary shows the policyholder's data, the vehicle's data and the chosen plan with its final price." | The summary shows, from the typed step 1 output re-derived on entry (US-02-Q-17) and the field configuration of this page load: one row per configured field that has a non-empty value, except `checkbox` fields, with the field's Strapi `label` and its display value (US-03-Q-05). Rows are grouped under "Tu vehículo" (reserved keys `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`) and "Tus datos" (every other key), each in `sortOrder`; a group with no rows is not shown. Display values: `select` → the option's Strapi label; `date` → long Spanish date from the country's `locale` ("15 de mayo de 1990"); `number` → digits with no grouping ("2022"); `text` → as entered (trimmed), except `documentNumber` (BR-02). The chosen plan (`plan.key`) is shown with its name, short description and final price `calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step 1 output, today)` (ADR-0007), formatted as in US-02-BR-03 with the caption "Precio anual" (US-03-Q-14). | US-03-AC-01, US-03-AC-06 |
| US-03-BR-02 | Story: "The document number is shown partially masked." | The value of the reserved key `documentNumber` is shown masked (US-03-Q-04): let *n* be the number of letters and digits in the value; the last *k* = min(4, ⌊n/2⌋) letters and digits stay visible, every earlier letter or digit becomes "•" (U+2022), and every other character (dots, dashes, spaces) stays in place. The same function applies to every country (no country branch). The full number never appears in the DOM, the document title, the URL or a log on the summary or confirmation. The rule applies only to `documentNumber`. | US-03-AC-05 |
| US-03-BR-03 | Story: "From the summary the person can go back to edit their data or change the plan." | "Editar mis datos" navigates to `/<country>/datos` and "Cambiar plan" to `/<country>/planes`, each as a new history entry. Step 1 values and the chosen plan are kept (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-07). The person returns to the summary through the normal flow (step 1 "Continuar" → step 2 → "Continuar"); the price is recomputed. Leaving the summary discards the terms acceptance and the payment simulation choice (US-03-Q-10, Q-11). Both actions are unavailable during a payment attempt (BR-05). | US-03-AC-07 |
| US-03-BR-04 | Story: "The pay button is enabled only after accepting the terms and conditions." | "Pagar" is enabled if and only if the terms of the country are shown (loaded and well-formed) **and** "Acepto los términos y condiciones" is checked **and** no payment attempt is in progress. Otherwise it is perceivably disabled (`aria-disabled="true"`, stays focusable), activating it does nothing, and the reason is shown next to it and linked to it (US-03-Q-17). Unchecking disables it again. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-08, US-03-AC-12 |
| US-03-BR-05 | Story: "The payment cannot be submitted twice." | One activation of an enabled "Pagar" starts exactly one payment attempt. From that moment until the outcome, "Pagar" is disabled and reads "Procesando pago…", the terms checkbox, the simulation choice, "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" are unavailable, and further activations (click, Enter, Space, repeated quickly) start no other attempt. After a success no further attempt is possible; after a rejection a new attempt is possible (BR-08). | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-09 |
| US-03-BR-06 | Story: "On successful payment, a confirmation with a simulated quote number is shown." | On a successful attempt the wizard state is deleted (the `quote-wizard` entry and the store's in-memory state; ADR-0003: "Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown") and then the confirmation is shown with a quote number of the format `COT-<country code>-<YYYYMMDD of today>-<6 digits>` (US-03-Q-07), kept in memory only. After that, a reload or the browser back action leads to an empty step 1 of the same country through the existing guards. | US-03-AC-03, US-03-AC-10, US-03-AC-11 |
| US-03-BR-07 | Story context: "accept the terms and conditions, whose text varies by country and is managed by the business team from Strapi." | The summary shows the terms of the current country: the published terms documents related to that country, the most recently published one if there are several, skipping malformed ones (US-03-Q-12). Draft-only terms and terms of other countries are never shown, and no anonymous caller can read drafts (ADR-0002). Publishing a change is reflected on the next full page load with no code change. The text keeps its formatting (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic) and is rendered without executing anything an editor typed (US-03-Q-02). No terms text exists in front-end code. | US-03-AC-02, US-03-AC-12, US-03-AC-13, US-03-AC-14, US-03-AC-19 |
| US-03-BR-08 | Story context: "Payment is simulated for this test." Story scenario "Rejected payment". Assessment: "Payment is simulated: a button that leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data." | The payment runs entirely in the browser, sends no request and asks for no card, bank or personal data. Its outcome is deterministic and selectable (proposed: a visible "Simulación de pago" choice, US-03-Q-01, ADR needed); processing takes a fixed simulated time (proposed 1.5 s). A rejected attempt shows a clear message, clears nothing (ADR-0003: "Rejected payment: Nothing cleared"), keeps the terms accepted and the simulation choice, and lets the person retry. | US-03-AC-04, US-03-AC-15, US-03-AC-19 |

## 5. Acceptance criteria

Conventions for every scenario:

- "I completed step 1 in Colombia" means the values of US-01-AC-04; "in Chile" means the values in
  the US-02 spec §5 conventions (RUT "12.345.678-5", Nombre completo "Ana Prueba Ficticia", Fecha
  de nacimiento 1990-05-15, Ciudad "Santiago", Patente "BCDF12", Marca "Kia", Modelo "Rio 5",
  Año 2022, consent checked). All values are fictitious seed values.
- "I chose a plan" means "Plan Total" in Colombia and "Plan Protegido" in Chile, then "Continuar"
  on step 2. Today is pinned to **2026-11-21** (final prices $2.310.000 and $528.000, US-02-AC-07).
- Terms are the seed of [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md).
- "The simulated payment fails / succeeds" means the outcome of the simulated payment is set to
  rejected / approved. With the proposed default of US-03-Q-01 that is the "Simulación de pago"
  choice "Pago rechazado" / "Pago aprobado"; if the ADR decides another mechanism, only this
  convention changes.
- Prices are compared with whitespace removed (US-02-BR-03). Code-owned copy is in §8.1.

### US-03-AC-01 — Complete summary

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Complete summary
  Given I completed step 1 in <country> and I chose a plan
  When I reach the summary
  Then the address is "/<code>/resumen" and I see the heading "Resumen de tu cotización"
  And under "Tus datos" I see, in this order: <holder rows>
  And under "Tu vehículo" I see, in this order: <vehicle rows>
  And under "Plan elegido" I see "<plan>", its short description and "<price>" with "Precio anual"

  Examples:
    | country  | code | holder rows | vehicle rows | plan | price |
    | Colombia | co | "Tipo de documento" "Cédula de ciudadanía"; "Número de documento" "••••••5678"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Medellín" | "Placa" "ABC123"; "Marca" "Mazda"; "Línea" "3 Touring"; "Modelo (año)" "2022" | Plan Total | $2.310.000 |
    | Chile    | cl | "RUT" "••.•••.678-5"; "Nombre completo" "Ana Prueba Ficticia"; "Fecha de nacimiento" "15 de mayo de 1990"; "Ciudad" "Santiago" | "Patente" "BCDF12"; "Marca" "Kia"; "Modelo" "Rio 5"; "Año" "2022" | Plan Protegido | $528.000 |
```

The consent checkbox is not listed (BR-01). The price equals the one shown on step 2 for the same
data and day (ADR-0007).

### US-03-AC-02 — Terms by country

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Terms by country
  Given I am on the summary in <country>
  When I view the terms and conditions
  Then I see the title "<title>" and the heading "<heading>" of the <country> terms in Strapi
  And I do not see "<other heading>"
  And the pay button is disabled until I accept them

  Examples:
    | country  | title                                                    | heading                 | other heading           |
    | Colombia | Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia     | Condiciones principales | Condiciones generales   |
    | Chile    | Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile     | Condiciones generales   | Condiciones principales |
```

### US-03-AC-03 — Successful payment

```gherkin
Scenario: Successful payment
  Given I am on the summary in Colombia and I accepted the terms
  And the simulated payment succeeds
  When I click pay
  Then the button is locked while the payment is processed: it is disabled and reads "Procesando pago…"
  And I see the confirmation heading "Pago confirmado"
  And I see "Tu número de cotización es" followed by a number matching ^COT-CO-20261121-\d{6}$
```

### US-03-AC-04 — Rejected payment

```gherkin
Scenario: Rejected payment
  Given I am on the summary in Chile and I accepted the terms
  And the simulated payment fails
  When I click pay
  Then I see the message "El pago fue rechazado y no se realizó ningún cobro. Puedes intentarlo de nuevo."
  And I am still on "/cl/resumen" with my data, "Plan Protegido" at "$528.000", and the terms still accepted
  And "Pagar" is enabled again
  When the simulated payment succeeds and I click pay
  Then I see the confirmation heading "Pago confirmado"
```

A reload after the rejection also keeps the data and the plan (ADR-0003); the terms acceptance is
reset by the reload (US-03-Q-10).

### US-03-AC-05 — Masked document number (derived from US-03-BR-02 / Q-04)

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Masked document number
  When the document number <value> is masked
  Then the shown text is <masked>
  And the accessible text is "Número oculto, termina en <tail>"

  Examples:
    | value          | masked         | tail   | why |
    | "1012345678"   | "••••••5678"   | 5678   | 10 digits, last 4 visible |
    | "12.345.678-5" | "••.•••.678-5" | 678-5  | separators stay in place |
    | "123456785"    | "•••••6785"    | 6785   | RUT typed without dots and dash |
    | "12345678-K"   | "•••••678-K"   | 678-K  | check digit K |
    | "12345678"     | "••••5678"     | 5678   | 8 characters |
    | "123456"       | "•••456"       | 456    | 6 characters: half visible |
    | "AB"           | "•B"           | B      | 2 characters |

## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

Logical model below; the physical model follows ADR-0001 (required `manyToOne` `country` relation,
`strictRelations: true` already set), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON) and the
`strapi-content-modeling` conventions. Names subject to US-03-Q-03.

### 7.1 Terms collection type (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Strapi type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | string, required, `maxLength: 150` | Spanish, non-blank. Shown as the terms heading and the region's accessible name. |
| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02 (proposed: `blocks`), required | Spanish formatted text. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` | ADR-0001; publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

No `key`, `sortOrder`, `isActive` or `version`: unpublishing is how an editor withdraws terms, and
the most recently published one wins (US-03-Q-12). No bespoke backend code (no uniqueness
middleware).

### 7.2 Wire shape and mapping

Request (one per summary entry and per "Reintentar", through the proxy, published only, 10 s
timeout):

```
GET /api/terms?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&fields[0]=title&fields[1]=body
  &fields[2]=publishedAt&sort[0]=publishedAt:desc&pagination[pageSize]=10
```

Mapping wire → logical `Terms` (boundary parser):

| Wire attribute | Valid when | Logical attribute |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | non-blank string | `title` |
| `body` | per the ADR of US-03-Q-02; with `blocks`: an array whose supported nodes yield at least one non-blank text | `blocks` (the whitelisted, typed node tree) |
| `publishedAt` | ISO date-time string | used for ordering only |

The parser sorts by `publishedAt` descending itself and does not rely on the server sort. A
malformed entry is skipped with a `console.warn` naming the problem, never the text.

### 7.3 Seed (summary)

Full text in the annex [seed-terms.md](seed-terms.md). Idempotent, natural key country code +
`title`.

| Country | Published | Draft only |
|---|---|---|
| CO | "Términos y condiciones del seguro de auto – Colombia" (5 blocks, bulleted list, heading "Condiciones principales") | "Términos y condiciones (borrador)" |
| CL | "Términos y condiciones del seguro automotriz – Chile" (5 blocks, numbered list, heading "Condiciones generales") | — |

### 7.4 Access (ADR-0002, ADR-0005)

- Public role: add exactly the terms `find` (`api::term.term.find` with the US-03-Q-03 default),
  reconciled in bootstrap; no `findOne`. Justification: the summary must show the country's terms

### 7.5 What US-03 reads from the wizard state and the page load

  **nothing** to the entry: no terms acceptance, simulation choice, payment data or quote number.
- From this page load's content: field configuration (labels, option labels, types, `sortOrder`),
  the offered plans (name, short description, `basePrice`), the country (`code`, `currencyCode`,
  `locale`) and the terms.
- On success, the whole entry is deleted and the store's in-memory step 1 values and plan are
  reset (BR-06).

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment: "The wizard can be completed using only the keyboard, and fields
  have accessible labels"):** focus on the heading on arrival and on confirmation, description
  lists for data, a named focusable terms region, a labelled checkbox, a named radio group, a
  perceivable disabled "Pagar" with its reason, alerts announced once (AC-16, AC-17). WCAG 2.2 AA;
  screen reader pass at HC3.
- **Responsive (Assessment: "Works on mobile and desktop"):** 320–1440 CSS px without horizontal
  scroll; one column on narrow screens; targets ≥ 24 × 24 CSS px (AC-18, manual).
- **Multi-country (Assessment: "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and
  Chile"):** no terms text, field label, plan, currency, date format or masking branch per country
  in front-end code; dates and prices use the country's `locale` and `currencyCode` from Strapi.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment: "No Strapi token with write permissions may reach the
  browser. Public role permissions minimal and justified"; "Use fictitious data only."):** one
  added public permission (§7.4); reads through the GET-only proxy; drafts never anonymous; no
  request during payment; no card data; masking at display time; no value, quote number or terms
  text in logs; rich text rendered without executing editor input (AC-13, AC-19). Seed and test
  data fictitious.
- **Persistence (Assessment: "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not
  required."):** ADR-0003 unchanged; US-03 adds nothing to storage and deletes the entry on success.
- **Performance:** one terms request per summary entry; summary data comes from content already
  loaded by the guards in this page load; the price rule and masking are synchronous pure functions.
- **Testing (Assessment: "Unit tests for the relevant logic and at least one e2e test of the full
  flow for one country"):** masking, value display, quote number, terms parser and the simulated
  payment are unit tested; the CO full-flow e2e is completed end to end (US-03-Q-16).
- **Language:** end-user copy Spanish; code, logs and docs English.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

9	# ADR-0007: Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	Step 2 shows each plan's **final price**: its base price adjusted by "a simulated rule based on
14	the step 1 data. The rule is documented." (US-02 story, US-02-BR-04). The summary of US-03 must
15	show the same price. Spec §7.6 proposes a starting rule (a driver-age factor and a vehicle-age
16	factor, integer arithmetic, round half up, neutral factor with a warning when an input is
17	missing). At HC1 the human answered US-02-Q-01: "decided by an ADR that weighs **real
18	alternatives** (for example, factors configurable in Strapi); the proposed rule is the starting
19	point" (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21). We must decide where the rule's formula and its numbers live,
20	where it runs, how it rounds, which "today" it uses, and how US-03 reuses it. Story: US-02
21	(`specs/US-02/spec.md` §4 BR-04, §5 AC-07, §7.6); consumer: US-03.
22	
23	## Decision Drivers
24	
25	- D1. "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected." and the rule
26	  "is documented" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-04). Simplicity is allowed; documentation is
27	  required.
28	- D2. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
29	  offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment."; evaluated as "form and plans 100%
30	  configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-06).
31	- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app"; "Each country has its own
32	  regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment; ADR-0001 D3,
33	  D4).
34	- D4. Step 1 values never leave the browser (source: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04,
35	  US-02-AC-19). The rule runs in the front end.
36	- D5. Public permissions minimal and justified; published content only; no write token in the
37	  browser (source: Assessment, security; ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005).
38	- D6. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum (source: human decision recorded as D3 in ADR-0005 and
39	  D4 in ADR-0006).
40	- D7. Deterministic, exact prices in whole units: COP and CLP have no decimals; the result is an
41	  integer ≥ 1 (source: US-02-BR-03, US-02-BR-04, US-02-Q-06, US-02-Q-07).
42	- D8. "Today" comes from the injectable clock of US-01-Q-06, so tests pin it (source: US-01 spec
43	  glossary; `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `CLOCK`).
44	- D9. Malformed content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names keys, never values,
45	  and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, CLAUDE.md §3).
46	- D10. US-03 shows the same final price the person chose (source: spec §7.4 "For US-03").
47	- D11. Do not destabilise US-01, which is Ready for QA (source: `specs/US-01/tasks.md`).
48	- D12. Scope and pace of US-02: the approved spec v0.1 describes a fixed rule; anything else
49	  reopens the spec (source: human decision at HC2, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).
50	
51	## Considered Options
52	
53	1. **A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function**: the §7.6 formula *and* its factors are typed
54	   constants in `price-rules.ts`, the same for both countries.
55	2. **B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`**: the formula stays in a pure
56	   front-end function; the two factor tables (driver age, vehicle age) are repeatable components
57	   on the existing `country` content type, edited in Strapi.
58	3. **C. Factor tables in a separate `pricing-rule` collection type** with a required `country`
59	   relation, its own draft & publish, router, permission and proxy path.
60	4. **D. Factor tables per plan**: the same two repeatable components on each `plan`, so each plan
61	   has its own sensitivity to age and vehicle age (a constant per-plan multiplier is discussed
62	   under this option).
63	5. **E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional per-country overrides in Strapi**: option A's
64	   constants apply unless the country entry carries tables.
65	
66	Not considered further, because they contradict an accepted ADR: computing the price in a custom
67	Strapi endpoint that receives `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (sends step 1 values to a server:
68	ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04); a free JSON or expression attribute holding the rule (ADR-0006
69	and the `strapi-content-modeling` skill forbid free JSON for editor-facing configuration).
70	
71	## Decision Outcome
72	
73	Chosen option: **"A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function"** (human decision at HC2, Felipe
74	Sabogal, 2026-11-21), because it meets the assessment's requirement for a simulated, documented
75	rule completely (D1) with the smallest change: one pure function that runs in the browser (D4),
76	is exact and deterministic (D7), takes "today" as a parameter (D8), and is reused as is by US-03
77	(D10). It adds no content type, attribute, request, permission or backend code (D5, D6), leaves
78	the `country` type and the US-01 code untouched (D11), and is exactly what the approved spec v0.1
79	describes (D12). The cost, that the business cannot retune the factors without a deployment and
80	that both countries share them (D2, D3), is accepted; option B is the upgrade path.
81	
82	### What is decided
83	
84	**One pure function** (`frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, no Angular import, no
85	`new Date()`):
86	
87	```
88	calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step1Output, today) →
89	  driverAge     = completed years between step1Output.values.birthDate and today
90	                  (same reckoning as US-01-BR-04: 29 Feb birthdays turn on 1 Mar in non-leap years)
91	  vehicleAge    = max(0, year(today) − step1Output.values.vehicleYear)
92	  driverPct     = factorPercent of the DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS band containing driverAge, else 100
93	  vehiclePct    = factorPercent of the VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS band containing vehicleAge, else 100
94	  final         = max(1, floor((basePrice × driverPct × vehiclePct + 5000) / 10000))
95	```
96	
97	**Factors: typed constants in the same file** (spec §7.6, expressed as whole percentages):
98	
99	| `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` (completed years) | `factorPercent` | `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS` (years) | `factorPercent` |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| 18–25 | 120 | 0–5 | 110 |
102	| 26–60 | 100 | 6–10 | 100 |
103	| 61 and older | 110 | 11 and older | 90 |
104	
105	- Each table is a `readonly` array of `{ fromYears: number; toYears: number | null; factorPercent:
106	  number }` (`toYears: null` means "and older"), sorted, non-overlapping, and covered by a unit
107	  test that asserts exactly these rows. The names `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` and `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS`
108	  follow CLAUDE.md §6 (constants in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, in the file that owns them). The same
109	  constants apply to every country; no country code appears in the function.
110	- **Integer arithmetic.** Factors are integer **percentages** (`120` means ×1.20, `100` is
111	  neutral). With `basePrice ≤ 2 147 483 647` (US-02-BR-01) and the largest product of factors
112	  `120 × 110 = 13 200`, the numerator stays below about 2.84 × 10¹³, far below
113	  `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9 007 199 254 740 991; MDN: "'Safe' in this context refers to the
114	  ability to represent integers exactly and to compare them correctly"), so every step is exact
115	  in a JavaScript `number`. No floating-point factor is ever multiplied.
116	- **Rounding.** `floor((n + 5000) / 10000)` is round half up for the positive integers involved
117	  (49.5 → 50, 59.4 → 59; US-02-AC-07). The result is in whole units of the country's currency; it
118	  is never rounded to a currency-specific step (COP and CLP have no decimals, US-02-Q-07).
119	  Formatting stays `Intl.NumberFormat` with no fraction digits (US-02-BR-03).
120	- **Clock.** `today` is a parameter. Callers pass the value of the `CLOCK` injection token
121	  (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `InjectionToken<() => Date>`, US-01-Q-06). Tests pin it.
122	- **Missing inputs.** `birthDate` or `vehicleYear` absent from the typed step 1 output (an editor
123	  removed the reserved field) or `null` (an empty optional field) → that factor is `100` and a
124	  `console.warn` names the key (`birthDate`, `vehicleYear`), never the value (US-02-BR-04,
125	  US-01-Q-08).
126	- **No band matches** (only possible for a driver under 18, whom US-01-BR-04 and the step guard
127	  already keep out of step 2) → that factor is `100` and a `console.warn` names the table, never
128	  the age. This is defensive; it changes no AC.
129	- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.
130	- **Security.** Nothing changes: no request is added, no permission, router or proxy rule is
131	  touched, and no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19).
132	- **Reuse by US-03.** US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the typed step 1 output
133	  (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary shows the price step 2 showed,
134	  unless "today" or the plan's published base price changed between the two computations (a
135	  birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing a new base price before a reload); that is the
136	  intended behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).
137	
138	### Consequences
139	
140	- Good, because it is the smallest change that meets D1: one pure, exhaustively unit-testable
141	  function, with no schema, seed, request, parser or backend code (D6, D7).
142	- Good, because the documented rule is exactly the running rule: the numbers are in this ADR, in
143	  spec §7.6 and in one file, and cannot drift through content edits.
144	- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured in Strapi, and step 2 has no new failure mode.
145	- Good, because US-01 is untouched: no change to `country`, its request or its parser (D11), and
146	  no Strapi volume reset is needed.
147	- Good, because the approved spec v0.1 needs no revision, so step 3 (tests) can start (D12).
148	- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change, a review and a deployment (against D2) —
149	  mitigation: the factors are two small typed tables in one file; option B is the documented
150	  upgrade path, and the function's signature already isolates the tables, so moving them to
151	  content later changes the caller, not the formula.
152	- Bad, because Colombia and Chile get the same adjustment (against D3) — mitigation: the base
153	  prices, which dominate the final price, are already per country and content (US-02-BR-01); a
154	  per-country branch in code is forbidden (US-01-BR-07, ADR-0001), so per-country factors mean
155	  option B, not a code change.
156	- Neutral: pricing numbers in front-end code are not plan content (names, prices, coverages,
157	  benefits), so US-02-BR-06 ("No plan name, price, coverage or benefit exists in front-end code")
158	  still holds.
159	
160	### Strongest argument against
161	
162	Option B makes the factors content, per country, edited in Strapi and live on the next reload,
163	with no new permission, router, proxy path or backend code, because `country` is already public,
164	published-only and allow-listed. That is precisely what the assessment's evaluation criterion
165	rewards: "form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" and "Content differentiated by country".
166	Under option A, the price a Colombian or Chilean visitor sees depends on numbers that only a
167	developer can change, and they are the same in both countries. A business team that wants to
168	make young drivers cheaper in Chile only, or soften the surcharge on old cars after a campaign,
169	must ask for a deployment, which is the situation the business context of the assessment
170	describes as the problem to solve.
171	
172	**Why we accept it:** it is the human's decision for scope and pace (HC2, 2026-11-21). The
173	assessment explicitly allows a simulated price ("a real rating engine is not expected"), and the
174	approved spec v0.1 already describes this rule, so US-02 proceeds to tests without a spec
175	revision. Option A avoids a schema change on `country` (which US-01 depends on), a second request
176	with its own failure mode, a band parser with overlap and gap rules, a seed that cannot backfill
177	existing databases (a volume reset), and the quiet failure mode of a misconfigured band. The rule
178	stays fully documented in one place. Option B remains the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).
179	
180	### Confirmation
181	
182	- Unit tests `price-rules.spec.ts` (clock pinned to 2026-11-21): every US-02-AC-07 row; the two
183	  tables equal the §7.6 rows exactly; integer exactness at the bound (`basePrice` 2 147 483 647
184	  with the largest factors); result ≥ 1; missing and `null` inputs warn with the key and without
185	  the value.
186	- E2E (`full-flow-co`, `plans-cl-content`): the seed prices of US-02-AC-07 with the browser clock
187	  pinned; US-02-AC-13 recomputation after a changed vehicle year.
188	- Review checklist: `price-rules.ts` has no Angular import and no `new Date()`; factor literals
189	  appear only in `price-rules.ts` and its tests; no country code or per-country branch in the
190	  rule; US-03 imports `calculateFinalPrice` rather than copying it.
191	
192	## Pros and Cons of the Options
193	
194	### A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function (chosen)
195	
196	`price-rules.ts` holds both the formula and the §7.6 factors; US-03 imports it.
197	
198	- Good, because it is the smallest change: one pure function, no schema, seed, request or parser.
199	- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured, and the documented rule is exactly the running rule
200	  (D1).
201	- Good, because it has no new failure mode on step 2, and US-01 is untouched (D11).
202	- Good, because it matches the approved spec v0.1 (D12).
203	- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change and a deployment (against D2).
204	- Bad, because both countries get the same adjustment; differentiating them would need a
205	  per-country branch in code, which US-01-BR-07 and ADR-0001 forbid (against D3).
206	
207	### B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`
208	
209	New component `pricing.age-band` (`fromYears` integer `min: 0`, `toYears` optional integer,
210	`factorPercent` integer `min: 1`, `max: 1000`); `country` gains repeatable `driverAgeFactors` and
211	`vehicleAgeFactors`; step 2 loads them with a separate `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]=…`
212	request that populates the two components; the formula is the same as in A.
213	
214	- Good, because the numbers are content per country, editable without a deployment (D2, D3).
215	- Good, because it reuses the country's existing public `find`, `publishedOnlyConfig()` router
216	  and proxy path: components need no permission of their own (verified below) (D5, D6).
217	- Good, because the formula stays a documented pure function (D1, D7).
218	- Bad, because Strapi cannot validate band consistency (overlaps, gaps, `toYears < fromYears`;
219	  there is no cross-item validation of repeatable components, verified below), so the front end
220	  needs a band parser (D9), and a misconfigured band fails quietly as a neutral price.
221	- Bad, because the tables share draft & publish and the editing screen with the country entry
222	  that US-01 depends on.
223	- Bad, because step 2 makes a second request with its own failure mode, and the create-only seed
224	  cannot add the tables to an existing database (a volume reset).
225	- Bad, because the approved spec would need a revision (scope, contract, BR-04, BR-06, AC-11, §9).
226	
227	### C. Separate `pricing-rule` collection type
228	
229	One document per country with a required `country` relation and the same two repeatable
230	components.
231	
232	- Good, because pricing has its own draft & publish, history and admin entry, apart from the
233	  country's identity attributes.
234	- Good, because its permission could later differ from `country`'s.
235	- Bad, because it adds a public permission `api::pricing-rule.pricing-rule.find`, a router with
236	  `publishedOnlyConfig()`, a proxy allow-list entry, a bootstrap reconciliation change, and
237	  `country.find` for the relation filter (against D5, D6).
238	- Bad, because "exactly one rule per country" is not expressible in Strapi (`unique` is not
239	  scoped by relation, ADR-0001): it needs a Document Service middleware like the field-key one, or
240	  a front-end "first one wins" rule (against D6).
241	
242	### D. Factor tables per plan
243	
244	The two components on each `plan`, read in the plans request.
245	
246	- Good, because one request carries plans and factors: no second request and no new failure
247	  mode.
248	- Good, because a plan can price risk differently (a young-driver plan with a gentler age factor).
249	- Bad, because editors must repeat and keep in step the same tables on every plan of every
250	  country (six tables per country with the seed); a forgotten plan prices differently with no
251	  visible error.
252	- Bad, because it is more than the story asks: the rule is "based on the step 1 data", not per
253	  plan.
254	- Variant, a **constant per-plan multiplier**: it does not use step 1 data, so it is equivalent
255	  to editing `basePrice` and adds nothing to the rule.
256	
257	### E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional Strapi overrides
258	
259	- Good, because a fresh or misconfigured country still gets the documented factors instead of a
260	  neutral price.
261	- Bad, because there are two sources of truth: an editor cannot tell from the admin which numbers
262	  apply, and emptying a table brings back hidden code values instead of "no adjustment".
263	- Bad, because it carries all the Strapi-side cost of B plus the code tables of A.
264	
265	## Spec impact
266	
267	None. The approved spec v0.1 already describes option A (§7.6, US-02-BR-04, US-02-AC-07,
268	§11 `price-rules.spec.ts`), and its out-of-scope line "Price rule parameters edited in Strapi,
269	unless the ADR for US-02-Q-01 chooses that option" stays as written. Two details this ADR makes
270	precise do not change any AC: factors are written as whole percentages (120 for 1.20), which is
271	the "integer arithmetic" of §7.6; and the defensive neutral factor when no band matches is
272	unreachable through the UI. At the next spec revision, the header's *Related ADRs* can name
273	ADR-0007 instead of "Needed"; no revision is required for that.
274	
275	## More Information
276	
277	- Verified in the installed packages (versions from each `package.json`: `@strapi/core`,
278	  `@strapi/utils`, `@strapi/database`, `@strapi/strapi` 5.63.0 in `backend/node_modules`;
279	  `@angular/core`, `@angular/router` 22.3.0 in `frontend/node_modules`), on 2026-11-21. The Strapi
280	  facts support the assessment of options B to D:
281	  - Components need no read permission of their own: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
282	    `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` returns early unless
283	    `attribute.type === 'relation'`, and checks `<target>.find` only for relations.
284	  - A component can be populated with `fields`: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
285	    `dist/convert-query-params.js:367-385` resolves `attribute.type === 'component'` to the
286	    component schema and passes the sub-populate to `convertNestedPopulate`, which converts
287	    `fields` (lines 395-416).
288	  - Integer validation: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:322-328`
289	    (`yup.number().integer()`); `min` is skipped for drafts (lines 75-78), `max` always applies
290	    (lines 81-84).
291	  - Repeatable components: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js:35-44`
292	    and `92-110`: `min`/`max` on the list apply only when not a draft, and `min` only when the
293	    attribute is required or the list is non-empty. There is no cross-item validation.
294	  - `integer` is read back as a JavaScript number: `@strapi/database@5.63.0`
295	    `dist/fields/index.js:25` maps `integer` to the number field.
296	  - `CLOCK` exists as `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
297	- Strapi REST docs, "Populate and select" (https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select,
298	  read 2026-11-21): "The REST API by default does not populate any relations, media fields,
299	  components, or dynamic zones."
300	- MDN, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
301	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Number/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
302	  read 2026-11-21): value 9 007 199 254 740 991.
303	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (where country-level attributes would live under option B), ADR-0002 and
304	  ADR-0005 (unchanged), ADR-0003 (prices never stored), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON).
305	- Revisit when: the business needs to change the factors without a deployment, or needs different
306	  factors per country. The upgrade path is **option B** (per-country `pricing.age-band` tables on
307	  `country`), keeping `calculateFinalPrice`'s formula, rounding and fallbacks and passing the
308	  tables in as a parameter. Also revisit if plans need different sensitivities (option D), a rule
309	  input other than age and vehicle age is needed, or a real rating engine replaces the
310	  simulation.

# ADR-0007: Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function

## Context and Problem Statement

Step 2 shows each plan's **final price**: its base price adjusted by "a simulated rule based on
the step 1 data. The rule is documented." (US-02 story, US-02-BR-04). The summary of US-03 must
show the same price. Spec §7.6 proposes a starting rule (a driver-age factor and a vehicle-age
factor, integer arithmetic, round half up, neutral factor with a warning when an input is
missing). At HC1 the human answered US-02-Q-01: "decided by an ADR that weighs **real
alternatives** (for example, factors configurable in Strapi); the proposed rule is the starting
point" (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21). We must decide where the rule's formula and its numbers live,
where it runs, how it rounds, which "today" it uses, and how US-03 reuses it. Story: US-02
(`specs/US-02/spec.md` §4 BR-04, §5 AC-07, §7.6); consumer: US-03.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected." and the rule
  "is documented" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-04). Simplicity is allowed; documentation is
  required.
- D2. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
  offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment."; evaluated as "form and plans 100%
  configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-06).
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app"; "Each country has its own
  regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment; ADR-0001 D3,
  D4).
- D4. Step 1 values never leave the browser (source: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04,
  US-02-AC-19). The rule runs in the front end.
- D5. Public permissions minimal and justified; published content only; no write token in the
  browser (source: Assessment, security; ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005).
- D6. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum (source: human decision recorded as D3 in ADR-0005 and
  D4 in ADR-0006).
- D7. Deterministic, exact prices in whole units: COP and CLP have no decimals; the result is an
  integer ≥ 1 (source: US-02-BR-03, US-02-BR-04, US-02-Q-06, US-02-Q-07).
- D8. "Today" comes from the injectable clock of US-01-Q-06, so tests pin it (source: US-01 spec
  glossary; `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `CLOCK`).
- D9. Malformed content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names keys, never values,
  and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, CLAUDE.md §3).
- D10. US-03 shows the same final price the person chose (source: spec §7.4 "For US-03").
- D11. Do not destabilise US-01, which is Ready for QA (source: `specs/US-01/tasks.md`).
- D12. Scope and pace of US-02: the approved spec v0.1 describes a fixed rule; anything else
  reopens the spec (source: human decision at HC2, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).

## Considered Options

1. **A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function**: the §7.6 formula *and* its factors are typed
   constants in `price-rules.ts`, the same for both countries.
2. **B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`**: the formula stays in a pure
   front-end function; the two factor tables (driver age, vehicle age) are repeatable components
   on the existing `country` content type, edited in Strapi.
3. **C. Factor tables in a separate `pricing-rule` collection type** with a required `country`
   relation, its own draft & publish, router, permission and proxy path.
4. **D. Factor tables per plan**: the same two repeatable components on each `plan`, so each plan
   has its own sensitivity to age and vehicle age (a constant per-plan multiplier is discussed
   under this option).
5. **E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional per-country overrides in Strapi**: option A's
   constants apply unless the country entry carries tables.

Not considered further, because they contradict an accepted ADR: computing the price in a custom
Strapi endpoint that receives `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (sends step 1 values to a server:
ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04); a free JSON or expression attribute holding the rule (ADR-0006
and the `strapi-content-modeling` skill forbid free JSON for editor-facing configuration).

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function"** (human decision at HC2, Felipe
Sabogal, 2026-11-21), because it meets the assessment's requirement for a simulated, documented
rule completely (D1) with the smallest change: one pure function that runs in the browser (D4),
is exact and deterministic (D7), takes "today" as a parameter (D8), and is reused as is by US-03
(D10). It adds no content type, attribute, request, permission or backend code (D5, D6), leaves
the `country` type and the US-01 code untouched (D11), and is exactly what the approved spec v0.1
describes (D12). The cost, that the business cannot retune the factors without a deployment and
that both countries share them (D2, D3), is accepted; option B is the upgrade path.

### What is decided

**One pure function** (`frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, no Angular import, no
`new Date()`):

```
calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step1Output, today) →
  driverAge     = completed years between step1Output.values.birthDate and today
                  (same reckoning as US-01-BR-04: 29 Feb birthdays turn on 1 Mar in non-leap years)
  vehicleAge    = max(0, year(today) − step1Output.values.vehicleYear)
  driverPct     = factorPercent of the DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS band containing driverAge, else 100
  vehiclePct    = factorPercent of the VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS band containing vehicleAge, else 100
  final         = max(1, floor((basePrice × driverPct × vehiclePct + 5000) / 10000))
```

**Factors: typed constants in the same file** (spec §7.6, expressed as whole percentages):

| `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` (completed years) | `factorPercent` | `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS` (years) | `factorPercent` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 18–25 | 120 | 0–5 | 110 |
| 26–60 | 100 | 6–10 | 100 |
| 61 and older | 110 | 11 and older | 90 |

- Each table is a `readonly` array of `{ fromYears: number; toYears: number | null; factorPercent:
  number }` (`toYears: null` means "and older"), sorted, non-overlapping, and covered by a unit
  test that asserts exactly these rows. The names `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` and `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS`
  follow CLAUDE.md §6 (constants in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, in the file that owns them). The same
  constants apply to every country; no country code appears in the function.
- **Integer arithmetic.** Factors are integer **percentages** (`120` means ×1.20, `100` is
  neutral). With `basePrice ≤ 2 147 483 647` (US-02-BR-01) and the largest product of factors
  `120 × 110 = 13 200`, the numerator stays below about 2.84 × 10¹³, far below
  `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9 007 199 254 740 991; MDN: "'Safe' in this context refers to the
  ability to represent integers exactly and to compare them correctly"), so every step is exact
  in a JavaScript `number`. No floating-point factor is ever multiplied.
- **Rounding.** `floor((n + 5000) / 10000)` is round half up for the positive integers involved
  (49.5 → 50, 59.4 → 59; US-02-AC-07). The result is in whole units of the country's currency; it
  is never rounded to a currency-specific step (COP and CLP have no decimals, US-02-Q-07).
  Formatting stays `Intl.NumberFormat` with no fraction digits (US-02-BR-03).
- **Clock.** `today` is a parameter. Callers pass the value of the `CLOCK` injection token
  (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `InjectionToken<() => Date>`, US-01-Q-06). Tests pin it.
- **Missing inputs.** `birthDate` or `vehicleYear` absent from the typed step 1 output (an editor
  removed the reserved field) or `null` (an empty optional field) → that factor is `100` and a
  `console.warn` names the key (`birthDate`, `vehicleYear`), never the value (US-02-BR-04,
  US-01-Q-08).
- **No band matches** (only possible for a driver under 18, whom US-01-BR-04 and the step guard
  already keep out of step 2) → that factor is `100` and a `console.warn` names the table, never
  the age. This is defensive; it changes no AC.
- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.
- **Security.** Nothing changes: no request is added, no permission, router or proxy rule is
  touched, and no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19).
- **Reuse by US-03.** US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the typed step 1 output
  (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary shows the price step 2 showed,
  unless "today" or the plan's published base price changed between the two computations (a
  birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing a new base price before a reload); that is the
  intended behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).

### Consequences

- Good, because it is the smallest change that meets D1: one pure, exhaustively unit-testable
  function, with no schema, seed, request, parser or backend code (D6, D7).
- Good, because the documented rule is exactly the running rule: the numbers are in this ADR, in
  spec §7.6 and in one file, and cannot drift through content edits.
- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured in Strapi, and step 2 has no new failure mode.
- Good, because US-01 is untouched: no change to `country`, its request or its parser (D11), and
  no Strapi volume reset is needed.
- Good, because the approved spec v0.1 needs no revision, so step 3 (tests) can start (D12).
- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change, a review and a deployment (against D2) —
  mitigation: the factors are two small typed tables in one file; option B is the documented
  upgrade path, and the function's signature already isolates the tables, so moving them to
  content later changes the caller, not the formula.
- Bad, because Colombia and Chile get the same adjustment (against D3) — mitigation: the base
  prices, which dominate the final price, are already per country and content (US-02-BR-01); a
  per-country branch in code is forbidden (US-01-BR-07, ADR-0001), so per-country factors mean
  option B, not a code change.
- Neutral: pricing numbers in front-end code are not plan content (names, prices, coverages,
  benefits), so US-02-BR-06 ("No plan name, price, coverage or benefit exists in front-end code")
  still holds.

### Strongest argument against

Option B makes the factors content, per country, edited in Strapi and live on the next reload,
with no new permission, router, proxy path or backend code, because `country` is already public,
published-only and allow-listed. That is precisely what the assessment's evaluation criterion
rewards: "form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" and "Content differentiated by country".
Under option A, the price a Colombian or Chilean visitor sees depends on numbers that only a
developer can change, and they are the same in both countries. A business team that wants to
make young drivers cheaper in Chile only, or soften the surcharge on old cars after a campaign,
must ask for a deployment, which is the situation the business context of the assessment
describes as the problem to solve.

**Why we accept it:** it is the human's decision for scope and pace (HC2, 2026-11-21). The
assessment explicitly allows a simulated price ("a real rating engine is not expected"), and the
approved spec v0.1 already describes this rule, so US-02 proceeds to tests without a spec
revision. Option A avoids a schema change on `country` (which US-01 depends on), a second request
with its own failure mode, a band parser with overlap and gap rules, a seed that cannot backfill
existing databases (a volume reset), and the quiet failure mode of a misconfigured band. The rule
stays fully documented in one place. Option B remains the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `price-rules.spec.ts` (clock pinned to 2026-11-21): every US-02-AC-07 row; the two
  tables equal the §7.6 rows exactly; integer exactness at the bound (`basePrice` 2 147 483 647
  with the largest factors); result ≥ 1; missing and `null` inputs warn with the key and without
  the value.
- E2E (`full-flow-co`, `plans-cl-content`): the seed prices of US-02-AC-07 with the browser clock
  pinned; US-02-AC-13 recomputation after a changed vehicle year.
- Review checklist: `price-rules.ts` has no Angular import and no `new Date()`; factor literals
  appear only in `price-rules.ts` and its tests; no country code or per-country branch in the
  rule; US-03 imports `calculateFinalPrice` rather than copying it.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function (chosen)

`price-rules.ts` holds both the formula and the §7.6 factors; US-03 imports it.

- Good, because it is the smallest change: one pure function, no schema, seed, request or parser.
- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured, and the documented rule is exactly the running rule
  (D1).
- Good, because it has no new failure mode on step 2, and US-01 is untouched (D11).
- Good, because it matches the approved spec v0.1 (D12).
- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change and a deployment (against D2).
- Bad, because both countries get the same adjustment; differentiating them would need a
  per-country branch in code, which US-01-BR-07 and ADR-0001 forbid (against D3).

### B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`

New component `pricing.age-band` (`fromYears` integer `min: 0`, `toYears` optional integer,
`factorPercent` integer `min: 1`, `max: 1000`); `country` gains repeatable `driverAgeFactors` and
`vehicleAgeFactors`; step 2 loads them with a separate `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]=…`
request that populates the two components; the formula is the same as in A.

- Good, because the numbers are content per country, editable without a deployment (D2, D3).
- Good, because it reuses the country's existing public `find`, `publishedOnlyConfig()` router
  and proxy path: components need no permission of their own (verified below) (D5, D6).
- Good, because the formula stays a documented pure function (D1, D7).
- Bad, because Strapi cannot validate band consistency (overlaps, gaps, `toYears < fromYears`;
  there is no cross-item validation of repeatable components, verified below), so the front end
  needs a band parser (D9), and a misconfigured band fails quietly as a neutral price.
- Bad, because the tables share draft & publish and the editing screen with the country entry
  that US-01 depends on.
- Bad, because step 2 makes a second request with its own failure mode, and the create-only seed
  cannot add the tables to an existing database (a volume reset).
- Bad, because the approved spec would need a revision (scope, contract, BR-04, BR-06, AC-11, §9).

### C. Separate `pricing-rule` collection type

One document per country with a required `country` relation and the same two repeatable
components.

- Good, because pricing has its own draft & publish, history and admin entry, apart from the
  country's identity attributes.
- Good, because its permission could later differ from `country`'s.
- Bad, because it adds a public permission `api::pricing-rule.pricing-rule.find`, a router with
  `publishedOnlyConfig()`, a proxy allow-list entry, a bootstrap reconciliation change, and
  `country.find` for the relation filter (against D5, D6).
- Bad, because "exactly one rule per country" is not expressible in Strapi (`unique` is not
  scoped by relation, ADR-0001): it needs a Document Service middleware like the field-key one, or
  a front-end "first one wins" rule (against D6).

### D. Factor tables per plan

The two components on each `plan`, read in the plans request.

- Good, because one request carries plans and factors: no second request and no new failure
  mode.
- Good, because a plan can price risk differently (a young-driver plan with a gentler age factor).
- Bad, because editors must repeat and keep in step the same tables on every plan of every
  country (six tables per country with the seed); a forgotten plan prices differently with no
  visible error.
- Bad, because it is more than the story asks: the rule is "based on the step 1 data", not per
  plan.
- Variant, a **constant per-plan multiplier**: it does not use step 1 data, so it is equivalent
  to editing `basePrice` and adds nothing to the rule.

### E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional Strapi overrides

- Good, because a fresh or misconfigured country still gets the documented factors instead of a
  neutral price.
- Bad, because there are two sources of truth: an editor cannot tell from the admin which numbers
  apply, and emptying a table brings back hidden code values instead of "no adjustment".
- Bad, because it carries all the Strapi-side cost of B plus the code tables of A.

## Spec impact

None. The approved spec v0.1 already describes option A (§7.6, US-02-BR-04, US-02-AC-07,
§11 `price-rules.spec.ts`), and its out-of-scope line "Price rule parameters edited in Strapi,
unless the ADR for US-02-Q-01 chooses that option" stays as written. Two details this ADR makes
precise do not change any AC: factors are written as whole percentages (120 for 1.20), which is
the "integer arithmetic" of §7.6; and the defensive neutral factor when no band matches is
unreachable through the UI. At the next spec revision, the header's *Related ADRs* can name
ADR-0007 instead of "Needed"; no revision is required for that.

## More Information

- Verified in the installed packages (versions from each `package.json`: `@strapi/core`,
  `@strapi/utils`, `@strapi/database`, `@strapi/strapi` 5.63.0 in `backend/node_modules`;
  `@angular/core`, `@angular/router` 22.3.0 in `frontend/node_modules`), on 2026-11-21. The Strapi
  facts support the assessment of options B to D:
  - Components need no read permission of their own: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` returns early unless
    `attribute.type === 'relation'`, and checks `<target>.find` only for relations.
  - A component can be populated with `fields`: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
    `dist/convert-query-params.js:367-385` resolves `attribute.type === 'component'` to the
    component schema and passes the sub-populate to `convertNestedPopulate`, which converts
    `fields` (lines 395-416).
  - Integer validation: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/validators.js:322-328`
    (`yup.number().integer()`); `min` is skipped for drafts (lines 75-78), `max` always applies
    (lines 81-84).
  - Repeatable components: `@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/index.js:35-44`
    and `92-110`: `min`/`max` on the list apply only when not a draft, and `min` only when the
    attribute is required or the list is non-empty. There is no cross-item validation.
  - `integer` is read back as a JavaScript number: `@strapi/database@5.63.0`
    `dist/fields/index.js:25` maps `integer` to the number field.
  - `CLOCK` exists as `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
- Strapi REST docs, "Populate and select" (https://docs.strapi.io/cms/api/rest/populate-select,
  read 2026-11-21): "The REST API by default does not populate any relations, media fields,
  components, or dynamic zones."
- MDN, `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Number/MAX_SAFE_INTEGER,
  read 2026-11-21): value 9 007 199 254 740 991.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (where country-level attributes would live under option B), ADR-0002 and
  ADR-0005 (unchanged), ADR-0003 (prices never stored), ADR-0006 (typed attributes, no free JSON).
- Revisit when: the business needs to change the factors without a deployment, or needs different
  factors per country. The upgrade path is **option B** (per-country `pricing.age-band` tables on
  `country`), keeping `calculateFinalPrice`'s formula, rounding and fallbacks and passing the
  tables in as a parameter. Also revisit if plans need different sensitivities (option D), a rule
  input other than age and vehicle age is needed, or a real rating engine replaces the
  simulation.

2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence

8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.
218
