- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.

## Considered Options

1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
   tab close and successful payment.
3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
   memory only.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
clearing rules below (D4).

### What is decided

**Store and storage key**

- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
  lives only in the payment component's memory.
- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.

**When it is written**

- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.

**When it is read**

- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.

**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**

- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
  independent state.

**When it is cleared**

| Event | Effect | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |

**Privacy rules**

- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
  is never stored separately.
- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.

### Consequences

- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
  after a rejected payment (D6).
- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
  the data stays on the same device and profile.
- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.

### Strongest argument against

The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.

**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
  memory fallback.
- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
  request).
- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
  successful payment and not on a rejected one.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. In memory only

- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
  guard.

### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)

- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.

### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry

- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
  overwrite each other's state.

### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)

- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
  some fields.
- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.

## More Information

- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
  hydrated from the store).
- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
  required).
- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
  only on a valid Continuar.

8	
9	# ADR-0007: Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	Step 2 shows each plan's **final price**: its base price adjusted by "a simulated rule based on
14	the step 1 data. The rule is documented." (US-02 story, US-02-BR-04). The summary of US-03 must
15	show the same price. Spec §7.6 proposes a starting rule (a driver-age factor and a vehicle-age
16	factor, integer arithmetic, round half up, neutral factor with a warning when an input is
17	missing). At HC1 the human answered US-02-Q-01: "decided by an ADR that weighs **real
18	alternatives** (for example, factors configurable in Strapi); the proposed rule is the starting
19	point" (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21). We must decide where the rule's formula and its numbers live,
20	where it runs, how it rounds, which "today" it uses, and how US-03 reuses it. Story: US-02
21	(`specs/US-02/spec.md` §4 BR-04, §5 AC-07, §7.6); consumer: US-03.
22	
23	## Decision Drivers
24	
25	- D1. "Price calculation may be simulated: a real rating engine is not expected." and the rule
26	  "is documented" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-04). Simplicity is allowed; documentation is
27	  required.
28	- D2. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the
29	  offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment."; evaluated as "form and plans 100%
30	  configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment; US-02-BR-06).
31	- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app"; "Each country has its own
32	  regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment; ADR-0001 D3,
33	  D4).
34	- D4. Step 1 values never leave the browser (source: ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04,
35	  US-02-AC-19). The rule runs in the front end.
36	- D5. Public permissions minimal and justified; published content only; no write token in the
37	  browser (source: Assessment, security; ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005).
38	- D6. Keep bespoke backend code to a minimum (source: human decision recorded as D3 in ADR-0005 and
39	  D4 in ADR-0006).
40	- D7. Deterministic, exact prices in whole units: COP and CLP have no decimals; the result is an
41	  integer ≥ 1 (source: US-02-BR-03, US-02-BR-04, US-02-Q-06, US-02-Q-07).
42	- D8. "Today" comes from the injectable clock of US-01-Q-06, so tests pin it (source: US-01 spec
43	  glossary; `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `CLOCK`).
44	- D9. Malformed content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names keys, never values,
45	  and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, CLAUDE.md §3).
46	- D10. US-03 shows the same final price the person chose (source: spec §7.4 "For US-03").
47	- D11. Do not destabilise US-01, which is Ready for QA (source: `specs/US-01/tasks.md`).
48	- D12. Scope and pace of US-02: the approved spec v0.1 describes a fixed rule; anything else
49	  reopens the spec (source: human decision at HC2, Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21).
50	
51	## Considered Options
52	
53	1. **A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function**: the §7.6 formula *and* its factors are typed
54	   constants in `price-rules.ts`, the same for both countries.
55	2. **B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`**: the formula stays in a pure
56	   front-end function; the two factor tables (driver age, vehicle age) are repeatable components
57	   on the existing `country` content type, edited in Strapi.
58	3. **C. Factor tables in a separate `pricing-rule` collection type** with a required `country`
59	   relation, its own draft & publish, router, permission and proxy path.
60	4. **D. Factor tables per plan**: the same two repeatable components on each `plan`, so each plan
61	   has its own sensitivity to age and vehicle age (a constant per-plan multiplier is discussed
62	   under this option).
63	5. **E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional per-country overrides in Strapi**: option A's
64	   constants apply unless the country entry carries tables.
65	
66	Not considered further, because they contradict an accepted ADR: computing the price in a custom
67	Strapi endpoint that receives `birthDate` and `vehicleYear` (sends step 1 values to a server:
68	ADR-0002, ADR-0003, US-02-BR-04); a free JSON or expression attribute holding the rule (ADR-0006
69	and the `strapi-content-modeling` skill forbid free JSON for editor-facing configuration).
70	
71	## Decision Outcome
72	
73	Chosen option: **"A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function"** (human decision at HC2, Felipe
74	Sabogal, 2026-11-21), because it meets the assessment's requirement for a simulated, documented
75	rule completely (D1) with the smallest change: one pure function that runs in the browser (D4),
76	is exact and deterministic (D7), takes "today" as a parameter (D8), and is reused as is by US-03
77	(D10). It adds no content type, attribute, request, permission or backend code (D5, D6), leaves
78	the `country` type and the US-01 code untouched (D11), and is exactly what the approved spec v0.1
79	describes (D12). The cost, that the business cannot retune the factors without a deployment and
80	that both countries share them (D2, D3), is accepted; option B is the upgrade path.
81	
82	### What is decided
83	
84	**One pure function** (`frontend/src/app/shared/price-rules.ts`, no Angular import, no
85	`new Date()`):
86	
87	```
88	calculateFinalPrice(basePrice, step1Output, today) →
89	  driverAge     = completed years between step1Output.values.birthDate and today
90	                  (same reckoning as US-01-BR-04: 29 Feb birthdays turn on 1 Mar in non-leap years)
91	  vehicleAge    = max(0, year(today) − step1Output.values.vehicleYear)
92	  driverPct     = factorPercent of the DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS band containing driverAge, else 100
93	  vehiclePct    = factorPercent of the VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS band containing vehicleAge, else 100
94	  final         = max(1, floor((basePrice × driverPct × vehiclePct + 5000) / 10000))
95	```
96	
97	**Factors: typed constants in the same file** (spec §7.6, expressed as whole percentages):
98	
99	| `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` (completed years) | `factorPercent` | `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS` (years) | `factorPercent` |
100	|---|---|---|---|
101	| 18–25 | 120 | 0–5 | 110 |
102	| 26–60 | 100 | 6–10 | 100 |
103	| 61 and older | 110 | 11 and older | 90 |
104	
105	- Each table is a `readonly` array of `{ fromYears: number; toYears: number | null; factorPercent:
106	  number }` (`toYears: null` means "and older"), sorted, non-overlapping, and covered by a unit
107	  test that asserts exactly these rows. The names `DRIVER_AGE_FACTORS` and `VEHICLE_AGE_FACTORS`
108	  follow CLAUDE.md §6 (constants in `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`, in the file that owns them). The same
109	  constants apply to every country; no country code appears in the function.
110	- **Integer arithmetic.** Factors are integer **percentages** (`120` means ×1.20, `100` is
111	  neutral). With `basePrice ≤ 2 147 483 647` (US-02-BR-01) and the largest product of factors
112	  `120 × 110 = 13 200`, the numerator stays below about 2.84 × 10¹³, far below
113	  `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (9 007 199 254 740 991; MDN: "'Safe' in this context refers to the
114	  ability to represent integers exactly and to compare them correctly"), so every step is exact
115	  in a JavaScript `number`. No floating-point factor is ever multiplied.
116	- **Rounding.** `floor((n + 5000) / 10000)` is round half up for the positive integers involved
117	  (49.5 → 50, 59.4 → 59; US-02-AC-07). The result is in whole units of the country's currency; it
118	  is never rounded to a currency-specific step (COP and CLP have no decimals, US-02-Q-07).
119	  Formatting stays `Intl.NumberFormat` with no fraction digits (US-02-BR-03).
120	- **Clock.** `today` is a parameter. Callers pass the value of the `CLOCK` injection token
121	  (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`, `InjectionToken<() => Date>`, US-01-Q-06). Tests pin it.
122	- **Missing inputs.** `birthDate` or `vehicleYear` absent from the typed step 1 output (an editor
123	  removed the reserved field) or `null` (an empty optional field) → that factor is `100` and a
124	  `console.warn` names the key (`birthDate`, `vehicleYear`), never the value (US-02-BR-04,
125	  US-01-Q-08).
126	- **No band matches** (only possible for a driver under 18, whom US-01-BR-04 and the step guard
127	  already keep out of step 2) → that factor is `100` and a `console.warn` names the table, never
128	  the age. This is defensive; it changes no AC.
129	- The function is synchronous and has no side effects other than the warnings.
130	- **Security.** Nothing changes: no request is added, no permission, router or proxy rule is
131	  touched, and no step 1 value is sent (US-02-AC-19).
132	- **Reuse by US-03.** US-03 imports the same `calculateFinalPrice`, the typed step 1 output
133	  (re-derived as in US-02-Q-17) and the same `CLOCK`. The summary shows the price step 2 showed,
134	  unless "today" or the plan's published base price changed between the two computations (a
135	  birthday at midnight, or an editor publishing a new base price before a reload); that is the
136	  intended behaviour of a recomputed, never-stored price (ADR-0003, US-02-BR-06).
137	
138	### Consequences
139	
140	- Good, because it is the smallest change that meets D1: one pure, exhaustively unit-testable
141	  function, with no schema, seed, request, parser or backend code (D6, D7).
142	- Good, because the documented rule is exactly the running rule: the numbers are in this ADR, in
143	  spec §7.6 and in one file, and cannot drift through content edits.
144	- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured in Strapi, and step 2 has no new failure mode.
145	- Good, because US-01 is untouched: no change to `country`, its request or its parser (D11), and
146	  no Strapi volume reset is needed.
147	- Good, because the approved spec v0.1 needs no revision, so step 3 (tests) can start (D12).
148	- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change, a review and a deployment (against D2) —
149	  mitigation: the factors are two small typed tables in one file; option B is the documented
150	  upgrade path, and the function's signature already isolates the tables, so moving them to
151	  content later changes the caller, not the formula.
152	- Bad, because Colombia and Chile get the same adjustment (against D3) — mitigation: the base
153	  prices, which dominate the final price, are already per country and content (US-02-BR-01); a
154	  per-country branch in code is forbidden (US-01-BR-07, ADR-0001), so per-country factors mean
155	  option B, not a code change.
156	- Neutral: pricing numbers in front-end code are not plan content (names, prices, coverages,
157	  benefits), so US-02-BR-06 ("No plan name, price, coverage or benefit exists in front-end code")
158	  still holds.
159	
160	### Strongest argument against
161	
162	Option B makes the factors content, per country, edited in Strapi and live on the next reload,
163	with no new permission, router, proxy path or backend code, because `country` is already public,
164	published-only and allow-listed. That is precisely what the assessment's evaluation criterion
165	rewards: "form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" and "Content differentiated by country".
166	Under option A, the price a Colombian or Chilean visitor sees depends on numbers that only a
167	developer can change, and they are the same in both countries. A business team that wants to
168	make young drivers cheaper in Chile only, or soften the surcharge on old cars after a campaign,
169	must ask for a deployment, which is the situation the business context of the assessment
170	describes as the problem to solve.
171	
172	**Why we accept it:** it is the human's decision for scope and pace (HC2, 2026-11-21). The
173	assessment explicitly allows a simulated price ("a real rating engine is not expected"), and the
174	approved spec v0.1 already describes this rule, so US-02 proceeds to tests without a spec
175	revision. Option A avoids a schema change on `country` (which US-01 depends on), a second request
176	with its own failure mode, a band parser with overlap and gap rules, a seed that cannot backfill
177	existing databases (a volume reset), and the quiet failure mode of a misconfigured band. The rule
178	stays fully documented in one place. Option B remains the upgrade path (see *Revisit when*).
179	
180	### Confirmation
181	
182	- Unit tests `price-rules.spec.ts` (clock pinned to 2026-11-21): every US-02-AC-07 row; the two
183	  tables equal the §7.6 rows exactly; integer exactness at the bound (`basePrice` 2 147 483 647
184	  with the largest factors); result ≥ 1; missing and `null` inputs warn with the key and without
185	  the value.
186	- E2E (`full-flow-co`, `plans-cl-content`): the seed prices of US-02-AC-07 with the browser clock
187	  pinned; US-02-AC-13 recomputation after a changed vehicle year.
188	- Review checklist: `price-rules.ts` has no Angular import and no `new Date()`; factor literals
189	  appear only in `price-rules.ts` and its tests; no country code or per-country branch in the
190	  rule; US-03 imports `calculateFinalPrice` rather than copying it.
191	
192	## Pros and Cons of the Options
193	
194	### A. Fixed rule in a pure front-end function (chosen)
195	
196	`price-rules.ts` holds both the formula and the §7.6 factors; US-03 imports it.
197	
198	- Good, because it is the smallest change: one pure function, no schema, seed, request or parser.
199	- Good, because nothing can be misconfigured, and the documented rule is exactly the running rule
200	  (D1).
201	- Good, because it has no new failure mode on step 2, and US-01 is untouched (D11).
202	- Good, because it matches the approved spec v0.1 (D12).
203	- Bad, because changing a factor needs a code change and a deployment (against D2).
204	- Bad, because both countries get the same adjustment; differentiating them would need a
205	  per-country branch in code, which US-01-BR-07 and ADR-0001 forbid (against D3).
206	
207	### B. Factor tables as per-country content on `country`
208	
209	New component `pricing.age-band` (`fromYears` integer `min: 0`, `toYears` optional integer,
210	`factorPercent` integer `min: 1`, `max: 1000`); `country` gains repeatable `driverAgeFactors` and
211	`vehicleAgeFactors`; step 2 loads them with a separate `GET /api/countries?filters[code][$eq]=…`
212	request that populates the two components; the formula is the same as in A.
213	
214	- Good, because the numbers are content per country, editable without a deployment (D2, D3).
215	- Good, because it reuses the country's existing public `find`, `publishedOnlyConfig()` router
216	  and proxy path: components need no permission of their own (verified below) (D5, D6).
217	- Good, because the formula stays a documented pure function (D1, D7).
218	- Bad, because Strapi cannot validate band consistency (overlaps, gaps, `toYears < fromYears`;
219	  there is no cross-item validation of repeatable components, verified below), so the front end
220	  needs a band parser (D9), and a misconfigured band fails quietly as a neutral price.
221	- Bad, because the tables share draft & publish and the editing screen with the country entry
222	  that US-01 depends on.
223	- Bad, because step 2 makes a second request with its own failure mode, and the create-only seed
224	  cannot add the tables to an existing database (a volume reset).
225	- Bad, because the approved spec would need a revision (scope, contract, BR-04, BR-06, AC-11, §9).
226	
227	### C. Separate `pricing-rule` collection type
228	
229	One document per country with a required `country` relation and the same two repeatable
230	components.
231	
232	- Good, because pricing has its own draft & publish, history and admin entry, apart from the
233	  country's identity attributes.
234	- Good, because its permission could later differ from `country`'s.
235	- Bad, because it adds a public permission `api::pricing-rule.pricing-rule.find`, a router with
236	  `publishedOnlyConfig()`, a proxy allow-list entry, a bootstrap reconciliation change, and
237	  `country.find` for the relation filter (against D5, D6).
238	- Bad, because "exactly one rule per country" is not expressible in Strapi (`unique` is not
239	  scoped by relation, ADR-0001): it needs a Document Service middleware like the field-key one, or
240	  a front-end "first one wins" rule (against D6).
241	
242	### D. Factor tables per plan
243	
244	The two components on each `plan`, read in the plans request.
245	
246	- Good, because one request carries plans and factors: no second request and no new failure
247	  mode.
248	- Good, because a plan can price risk differently (a young-driver plan with a gentler age factor).
249	- Bad, because editors must repeat and keep in step the same tables on every plan of every
250	  country (six tables per country with the seed); a forgotten plan prices differently with no
251	  visible error.
252	- Bad, because it is more than the story asks: the rule is "based on the step 1 data", not per
253	  plan.
254	- Variant, a **constant per-plan multiplier**: it does not use step 1 data, so it is equivalent
255	  to editing `basePrice` and adds nothing to the rule.
256	
257	### E. Hybrid: code defaults with optional Strapi overrides
258	
259	- Good, because a fresh or misconfigured country still gets the documented factors instead of a
260	  neutral price.
261	- Bad, because there are two sources of truth: an editor cannot tell from the admin which numbers
262	  apply, and emptying a table brings back hidden code values instead of "no adjustment".
263	- Bad, because it carries all the Strapi-side cost of B plus the code tables of A.
264	
265	## Spec impact
266	
267	None. The approved spec v0.1 already describes option A (§7.6, US-02-BR-04, US-02-AC-07,
268	§11 `price-rules.spec.ts`), and its out-of-scope line "Price rule parameters edited in Strapi,
269	unless the ADR for US-02-Q-01 chooses that option" stays as written. Two details this ADR makes
270	precise do not change any AC: factors are written as whole percentages (120 for 1.20), which is
271	the "integer arithmetic" of §7.6; and the defensive neutral factor when no band matches is
272	unreachable through the UI. At the next spec revision, the header's *Related ADRs* can name
273	ADR-0007 instead of "Needed"; no revision is required for that.
274	
275	## More Information
276	
277	- Verified in the installed packages (versions from each `package.json`: `@strapi/core`,
278	  `@strapi/utils`, `@strapi/database`, `@strapi/strapi` 5.63.0 in `backend/node_modules`;
279	  `@angular/core`, `@angular/router` 22.3.0 in `frontend/node_modules`), on 2026-11-21. The Strapi
280	  facts support the assessment of options B to D:
281	  - Components need no read permission of their own: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
282	    `dist/validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` returns early unless
283	    `attribute.type === 'relation'`, and checks `<target>.find` only for relations.
284	  - A component can be populated with `fields`: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`

2	status: Accepted
3	date: 2026-11-20
4	decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (accepted at HC2, 2026-11-20), architect subagent (proposal)
5	consulted: specs/US-01/spec.md v0.2 (Approved), specs/US-02/story.md, specs/US-03/story.md, MDN Web Docs (Window.sessionStorage)
6	informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence
7	---
8	
9	# ADR-0003: Front-end persistence of the wizard state
10	
11	## Context and Problem Statement
12	
13	The wizard keeps the step 1 values (US-01), later the chosen plan (US-02), between steps and must
14	not send them to any server. The person must find their data when going back (US-01-AC-04,
15	US-01-AC-20) and, after a rejected payment, "try again without losing my information" (US-03
16	story). The values include personal data: the document number and the birth date. We must decide
17	where the state lives, what is stored, how it is scoped per country, and when it is cleared
18	(US-01-Q-15, answered "decided by the ADR; sessionStorage is the starting point", and
19	US-01-Q-02, default accepted).
20	
21	## Decision Drivers
22	
23	- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
24	- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
25	- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
26	- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
27	- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
28	- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
29	- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.
30	
31	## Considered Options
32	
33	1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
34	2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
35	   tab close and successful payment.
36	3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
37	4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
38	   memory only.
39	
40	## Decision Outcome
41	
42	Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
43	the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
44	partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
45	(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
46	clearing rules below (D4).
47	
48	### What is decided
49	
50	**Store and storage key**
51	
52	- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
53	  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
54	- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
55	  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
56	  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
57	  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
58	  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
59	  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
60	  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
61	  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
62	  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
63	- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
64	  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
65	  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
66	  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
67	- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
68	  lives only in the payment component's memory.
69	- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.
70	
71	**When it is written**
72	
73	- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
74	  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
75	  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
76	  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.
77	
78	**When it is read**
79	
80	- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
81	  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
82	  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
83	- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
84	  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
85	  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.
86	
87	**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**
88	
89	- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
90	  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
91	  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
92	- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
93	  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
94	  independent state.
95	
96	**When it is cleared**
97	
98	| Event | Effect | Owner |
99	|---|---|---|
100	| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
101	| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
102	| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
103	| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
104	| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |
105	
106	**Privacy rules**
107	
108	- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
109	  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
110	- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
111	  is never stored separately.
112	- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
113	  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
114	  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
115	- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
116	  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.
117	
118	### Consequences
119	
120	- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
121	  after a rejected payment (D6).
122	- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
123	- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
124	  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
125	- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
126	  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
127	  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
128	  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
129	- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
130	  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
131	  the data stays on the same device and profile.
132	- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
133	  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
134	  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
135	- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
136	  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
137	- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
138	  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.
139	
140	### Strongest argument against
141	
142	The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
143	tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
144	"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
145	session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
146	personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.
147	
148	**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
149	fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
150	back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
151	logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
152	device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
153	
154	### Confirmation
155	
156	- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
157	  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
158	  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
159	  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
160	  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
161	  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
162	  memory fallback.
163	- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
164	  request).
165	- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
166	  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
167	  successful payment and not on a rejected one.
168	
169	## Pros and Cons of the Options
170	
171	### 1. In memory only
172	
173	- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
174	- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
175	- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
176	  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
177	- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
178	  guard.
179	
180	### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)
181	
182	- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
183	- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
184	- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
185	- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.
186	
187	### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry
188	
189	- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
190	- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
191	  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
192	- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
193	  overwrite each other's state.
194	
195	### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)
196	
197	- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
198	- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
199	  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
200	  some fields.
201	- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
202	  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.
203	
204	## More Information
205	
206	- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
207	  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
208	  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
209	  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
210	- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
211	  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
212	  hydrated from the store).
213	- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
214	  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
215	  required).
216	- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
217	  only on a valid Continuar.

**1. Untrusted values and escaping**
- "To systematically block XSS bugs, Angular treats all values as untrusted by default."
- Interpolated content is escaped: "Interpolated content is always escaped"

**2. innerHTML sanitization**
- Angular "automatically sanitizes it, which removes the `script` element." In my own words, it strips the script but keeps safe markup such as `<b>`.

**3. bypassSecurityTrust\* methods**
- "If you trust a value that might be malicious, you are introducing a security vulnerability into your application."

**4. Content Security Policy**
- "Content Security Policy (CSP) is a defense-in-depth technique to prevent XSS." CSP is set through the server's `Content-Security-Policy` HTTP header.

**5. Trusted Types**
- "It is recommended that you use Trusted Types as a way to help secure your applications from cross-site scripting attacks." The page says it should be enforced through server-sent headers, and that apps should still be guarded by Angular's DomSanitizer on browsers without support.

toolu_01VhjWsabbABTBhjc5Cp2z5h.prompt: Quote verbatim the sentences about how assistive technologies treat content/live regions inside an element with aria-busy="true" (e.g., wait until busy is false before exposing changes).

content.content:
From the MDN page on `aria-busy`:

> "The `aria-busy` attribute with a value of `true` can be added to an element currently being updated or modified, to inform the assistive technology that it should wait until the modifications or changes are complete before exposing the content to the user."

> "When multiple parts of a live region need to be loaded before changes are announced to the user, set `aria-busy="true"` until loading is complete. Then set to `aria-busy="false"`. This prevents assistive technologies from announcing changes before updates are done."

> "`aria-live`'s value dictates whether the changes are announced immediately upon changing the value to `false`, or the assistive technology waits until the current task is complete before interrupting the user."

The page also describes a `feed` case:

> "If an element with [`feed`](/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Roles/feed_role) role has `aria-busy` set to `true`, the rendering changes that occur inside the feed will not be announced with the exception of user-initiated changes."

The page's example for switching the state from script:

```js
ariaLiveElement.ariaBusy = "false";
```

toolu_01MwvTuBJmxbmwLEAbDaHSzc.prompt: Quote verbatim what the page says about disabled elements and focus (not focusable, removed from tab order, what happens if focused element becomes disabled), and about aria-disabled as alternative.

content.content:
The page doesn't cover three of your four points: removal from the tab order, what happens when a focused element becomes disabled, and `aria-disabled`. Here is what it does say about focus and disabled elements:

**Focus and interaction**
> "The user can neither edit nor focus on the control, nor its form control descendants."

> "Often browsers gray out such controls and it won't receive any browsing events, like mouse clicks or focus-related ones."

> "The difference between `disabled` and [`readonly`] is that read-only controls can still function and are still focusable, whereas disabled controls cannot receive focus and are not submitted with the form and generally do not function as controls until they are enabled."

**Constraint validation**
> "If the element is `disabled`, then the element's value cannot receive focus and cannot be updated by the user, and does not participate in constraint validation."

**Inheritance from ancestors**
> "If this attribute is not specified, the control inherits its setting from the containing element, for example `fieldset`; if there is no containing element with the `disabled` attribute set, and the control itself does not have the attribute, then the control is enabled."

> "If a [`<fieldset>`] is disabled, the descendant form controls are all disabled, with the exception of form controls within the [`<legend>`]."

**Pseudo-classes**
> "When a supporting element has the `disabled` attribute applied, the [`:disabled`] pseudo-class also applies to it. Conversely, elements that support the `disabled` attribute but don't have the attribute set match the [`:enabled`] pseudo-class."

**Not covered on the page:**
- Whether a disabled element is removed from the tab order (the page only says it "cannot receive focus").
- What happens to focus if the focused element is disabled while it has focus.
- `aria-disabled` as an alternative. The page never mentions it.

For the missing points, consult the HTML specification or the WAI-ARIA specification directly. Be aware that `aria-disabled` only conveys state to assistive technology and does not block focus, clicks, or form submission by itself, so it isn't a drop-in replacement for `disabled`.

# ADR-0008: Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data

## Context and Problem Statement

US-03 ends the wizard with a payment. The assessment says: "Payment is simulated: a button that
leads to a confirmation screen or a mock gateway. Do not integrate real payment gateways or use
real card data." The story has a "Rejected payment" scenario ("Given … the simulated payment
fails, When I click pay"), and the same build serves users and tests, so the rejected path must be
reachable in the production build without a test-only switch. We must decide where the outcome
comes from, how long processing takes and how tests control it, which boundary a real gateway
would later replace, how double submission is prevented, what the quote number is, what is cleared,
how the processing state is announced, and how "no real card data" is guaranteed and checked. The
human accepted the spec's proposal at HC1 (US-03-Q-01: "OK", Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) and asked
for it to be weighed against real alternatives. Story: US-03 (`specs/US-03/spec.md` §4 BR-05,
BR-06, BR-08; §6 US-03-Q-01).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Payment is simulated … Do not integrate real payment gateways or use real card data."
  (source: Assessment; US-03-BR-08).
- D2. The rejected path is testable with the same build, end to end, and deterministically
  (source: story "Rejected payment"; US-03-AC-04, US-03-BR-08; Assessment: "the same application
  and the same build serve Colombia and Chile").
- D3. "The payment cannot be submitted twice." (source: story; US-03-BR-05, US-03-AC-09).
- D4. Success deletes the wizard state before the confirmation; rejection clears nothing; payment
  data is never stored (source: ADR-0003; US-03-BR-06, BR-08, Q-10).
- D5. No personal data leaves the browser; reads only, through the GET-only proxy; no write path
  for anonymous callers (source: ADR-0002 as amended by ADR-0005; US-03-AC-19).
- D6. Keyboard-only use and perceivable states: the disabled pay button explains why, the
  processing and rejection states are announced once (source: Assessment, accessibility;
  US-03-AC-16, AC-17, Q-17; `review-checklist`: "Disabled pay button: its state is perceivable").
- D7. Unit tests control time and randomness; "today" comes from the injectable `CLOCK`
  (source: Assessment, testing; US-01-Q-06; ADR-0007 D8; US-03-Q-07).
- D8. Smallest change: no new route, guard, dependency or backend code (source: human decisions
  recorded as D3 in ADR-0005, D4 in ADR-0006, D12 in ADR-0007; US-03-Q-06 keeps the
  confirmation on `/:country/resumen`).
- D9. A real gateway can later replace the simulation in one place (source: US-03-Q-01, "It is a
  design that a real gateway would later replace").

## Considered Options

1. **A. Visible outcome choice on the summary**: a code-owned radio group "Simulación de pago (no
   se realiza ningún cobro)" with "Pago aprobado" (default) and "Pago rechazado", read when
   "Pagar" is activated, passed to a front-end simulated gateway that waits a fixed time and
   resolves; no card fields; no request.
2. **B. Mock gateway screen**: "Pagar" opens a gateway stand-in (a route such as
   `/:country/pago`, or a dialog) that shows the amount and two buttons, "Aprobar pago" and
   "Rechazar pago"; the outcome is chosen there.
3. **C. Deterministic rule on the input** ("magic values"): the outcome follows from the person's
   data, for example a document number or plate ending in a reserved value means "rejected"
   (variant: a hidden URL parameter such as `?pago=rechazado`).
4. **D. Random outcome**: a fixed share of attempts (for example 20 %) is rejected.
5. **E. Fictitious test card form**: card number, expiry and security code fields; reserved test
   numbers decide the outcome, as in real gateway sandboxes.

**Excluded, because it contradicts accepted ADRs: a backend mock endpoint** (for example
`POST /api/payments` in Strapi that answers approved or rejected). ADR-0002 makes the content API
read-only for the browser: the proxy forwards only `GET`/`HEAD` on an allow-list and answers `405`
to anything else, and the public role holds only `find` permissions. A payment endpoint needs a
write-like route open to anonymous callers, a new public permission or custom route, a proxy
exception for `POST`, and a request body carrying at least the plan and amount (US-03-AC-19
requires that no request contains the plan key or any step 1 value). It would also add bespoke
backend code for a simulation (against D8). Choosing it would need an ADR superseding ADR-0002.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. Visible outcome choice on the summary"**, because it is the only option that
is deterministic for both outcomes with the same build and no hidden behaviour (D2), asks for no
card data at all (D1), sends no request (D5), needs no new route, guard or dependency (D8), and
lets the story's scenario read as written: the outcome is set ("Given … fails") before the
activation ("When I click pay"). The gateway boundary (below) is what a real integration would
replace (D9).

### What is decided

**Outcome choice (code-owned copy, spec §8.1)**

- A `fieldset` with the `legend` "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún cobro)" and two native
  radio inputs, "Pago aprobado" (value `approved`, checked on arrival) and "Pago rechazado" (value
  `rejected`). Native radios give the radio group role, its accessible name from the legend, and
  arrow-key selection (US-03-AC-17).
- The choice lives in the page's memory only. It is never written to `sessionStorage`, the URL or
  a log (ADR-0003, US-03-Q-10). It is kept after a rejection and reset when the page is left or
  reloaded (US-03-BR-03, BR-08).
- The value is read **once**, when an attempt starts, and passed to the gateway. The group is
  disabled during the attempt, so it cannot change mid-attempt.

**Gateway boundary (the part a real gateway replaces, D9)**

- `frontend/src/app/core/payment-gateway.ts`: an abstract class `PaymentGateway` used as the DI
  token, with
  `pay(request: PaymentRequest, signal: AbortSignal): Promise<PaymentResult>`, where
  `PaymentRequest = { simulatedOutcome: 'approved' | 'rejected' }` and
  `PaymentResult = { status: 'approved' } | { status: 'rejected' }`. No amount, plan, country or
  personal value is passed: nothing that is not needed exists at the boundary.
- `frontend/src/app/core/simulated-payment-gateway.ts`: `SimulatedPaymentGateway`, provided as
  `{ provide: PaymentGateway, useClass: SimulatedPaymentGateway }`. It injects **no** `HttpClient`
  and no storage; it waits `SIMULATED_PROCESSING_MS = 1500` through the injected delay, then
  resolves to `{ status: request.simulatedOutcome }`. File names follow CLAUDE.md §6 (intent-
  revealing, no role suffix); the spec's `payment.spec.ts` is
  `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`.
- A real gateway would replace `SimulatedPaymentGateway` and `PaymentRequest` (it would carry a
  payment token from the provider's own hosted fields, never card data in this app), and remove
  the outcome choice. The page's states (processing, rejected, confirmed) stay.

**Injectable delay and clock (D7)**

- `PAYMENT_DELAY`: `InjectionToken<(ms: number, signal: AbortSignal) => Promise<void>>`, in
  `simulated-payment-gateway.ts`, default factory based on `setTimeout` and cleared on abort
  (the promise rejects with an `AbortError`). It must be timer-based, never a loop on `Date.now()`:
  the e2e tests pin the page clock with `page.clock.setFixedTime`, which (verified, playwright-core
  1.65.1 `types/types.d.ts`) "Makes `Date.now` and `new Date()` return fixed fake time at all
  times, keeps all the timers running", so a timer completes in 1.5 s while a `Date.now()` loop
  would never end.
- Unit and component tests either use Vitest fake timers (`vi.useFakeTimers()`,
  `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(1500)`, verified in vitest 5.1.1 `dist/index.d.ts`) or provide a
  controllable `PAYMENT_DELAY`.
- E2E tests keep the real 1.5 s (US-03-AC-15 measures it from the Node side, not with the page's
  pinned `Date`). They must not use `page.clock.install()` without `runFor`, because that also
  freezes timers.
- "Today" for the quote number comes from `CLOCK` (`frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`,
  `InjectionToken<() => Date>`), read when the approved result arrives; the date is the browser's
  local date (US-01-Q-06).

**Double-submit prevention (D3, US-03-BR-05)**

Three layers, each sufficient on its own for its case:

1. **Synchronous page guard.** The pay handler is bound to `(click)` only (a native `button`
   turns Enter and Space into one `click`; no extra key handlers). It returns at once unless
   `canPay()` holds (terms shown, accepted, state `idle` or `rejected`), and it sets the page state
   to `processing` **before** any `await`. A second click in the same task finds `processing`.
2. **Gateway in-flight flag.** `SimulatedPaymentGateway` holds a private `inFlight` flag; a `pay`
   call while it is set starts no timer and rejects with a `PaymentInProgressError` that the page
   ignores. This protects any future caller, not only this page.
3. **Perceivable lock.** During `processing`: "Pagar" keeps focus and reads "Procesando pago…",
   with `aria-disabled="true"` (not native `disabled`: MDN, "disabled controls cannot receive
   focus", which would drop the keyboard user's focus to the page body); the outcome `fieldset` and
   the terms checkbox are natively disabled; "Editar mis datos" and "Cambiar plan" are
   `aria-disabled="true"` and their handlers return early. `aria-disabled` does not block clicks by
   itself, so every handler checks the state.

After `approved`, the page state is `confirmed` and no handler starts another attempt. After
`rejected`, a new attempt is possible.

**Leaving during processing**

- The page owns an `AbortController`; `DestroyRef.onDestroy` aborts it. Browser back during an
  attempt destroys the page, the delay rejects, and **nothing** is cleared or shown (an attempt
  never completes on a page that is gone). A reload abandons the attempt the same way (US-03-Q-08).

**Simulated quote number (US-03-Q-07, AC-10)**

- Format `COT-<country code>-<YYYYMMDD>-<6 digits>`, for example `COT-CO-20261121-482913`.
  `COT` stands for *cotización*; the number is fictitious, not unique across sessions (one in a
  million per country and day), and the confirmation says the payment is simulated.
- `frontend/src/app/shared/quote-number.ts`: a pure `formatQuoteNumber(countryCode, today,
  digits)` (upper-case code, local `YYYYMMDD`, `digits` zero-padded to 6).
- `frontend/src/app/core/random-digits.ts`: `RANDOM_DIGITS`, `InjectionToken<() => number>`
  returning an integer in `[0, 999 999]`. The default uses `crypto.getRandomValues` on a
  `Uint32Array(1)` with rejection sampling (discard values ≥ 4 294 000 000, then `% 1 000 000`),
  so every value is equally likely. MDN: `getRandomValues()` "is the only member of the `Crypto`
  interface which can be used from an insecure context", so it works on the plain-HTTP
  `docker compose` stack. Tests provide a fixed source.
- The number is kept only in the page's memory: never stored, sent, logged, or put in the URL or
  the document title (US-03-AC-10).

**What is cleared and kept (ADR-0003, D4)**

| Outcome | Wizard state (`quote-wizard` entry and `QuoteStore` memory) | Page memory | Shown |
|---|---|---|---|
| Approved | **Deleted** through a new `QuoteStore` method (for example `clearQuote()`), which removes the entry and resets the in-memory step 1 values and plan, **before** the confirmation state is set | Quote number kept; terms acceptance and outcome choice discarded with the summary view | Confirmation (US-03-Q-13) |
| Rejected | **Nothing** cleared | Terms acceptance and outcome choice kept | Rejection message; "Pagar" enabled again |
| Abandoned (back, reload during processing) | Nothing cleared | Lost with the page | Whatever the navigation shows |

Order on approval: result → quote number (`CLOCK`, `RANDOM_DIGITS`) → `clearQuote()` → page
state `confirmed` → document title "Pago confirmado | Cotizador de seguro de auto" → focus on the
"Pago confirmado" heading after render (`afterNextRender`). Only `QuoteStore` touches
`sessionStorage` (ADR-0003). The confirmation is rendered by the same component, **not** in a
`@defer` block or a lazy chunk, so no request (not even a JavaScript chunk) is sent between the
activation and the confirmation (US-03-AC-15).

**Accessibility of the processing state (D6, US-03-AC-17)**

- The summary content gets `aria-busy="true"` during `processing`. MDN: `aria-busy="true"` tells
  assistive technology "to wait until the modifications or changes are complete before exposing
  the content". Therefore the status and alert regions are placed **outside** the busy subtree,
  or they would be held back.
- A polite `role="status"` region, outside the busy subtree and present from the start (empty),
  receives "Procesando pago…" once when the attempt starts and is emptied when it ends.
- On rejection: `aria-busy` is removed first, then the rejection message is rendered in a
  `role="alert"` region next to "Pagar" (outside the busy subtree); focus stays on "Pagar"
  (US-03-Q-09). The message is removed when a new attempt starts.
- On approval: focus moves to the confirmation heading and the title changes (US-03-AC-16).
- No animation is needed; if a spinner is added, it respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

**How "no real card data" is guaranteed (D1) and how a reviewer verifies it**

Guarantees by construction:

- The summary and confirmation contain exactly three form controls: the terms checkbox and the two
  outcome radios. No `input`, `select` or `textarea` exists for card, expiry, security code, bank
  or any personal data, and no element carries an `autocomplete` token starting with `cc-` (which
  would invite the browser to autofill a saved real card).
- `PaymentGateway`'s request type has no field that could hold card data; `SimulatedPaymentGateway`
  injects no `HttpClient`.
- No payment SDK or third-party script is added: `frontend/package.json` dependencies are
  unchanged by US-03.
- The proxy and Strapi are unchanged except for the terms read path (spec §7.4).

Checks:

- Component test (`summary-page.spec.ts`, US-03-AC-15): the page's `input`, `select` and
  `textarea` elements are exactly one checkbox and two radios; no `autocomplete^="cc-"`.
- Unit test (`simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`): with `provideHttpClientTesting()`,
  `HttpTestingController.verify()` passes after an approved and a rejected attempt; the result
  arrives at 1500 ms and not before; a second `pay` during an attempt starts no timer; abort
  rejects and starts nothing.
- E2E (`full-flow-co`, US-03-AC-15, AC-19): `page.on('request')` records **zero** requests between
  the activation of "Pagar" and the confirmation heading.
- Review: `grep -rniE "cc-(number|exp|csc)|card|tarjeta|cvv|cvc|iban" frontend/src` returns no
  match outside copy that says no charge is made; `git diff main -- frontend/package.json` shows no
  new dependency.

### Consequences

- Good, because both outcomes are reachable deterministically, by users and tests, with the same
  build and no hidden switch (D2).
- Good, because no card data can be entered: there is nowhere to type it, and no browser autofill
  target exists (D1).
- Good, because nothing is sent: the payment adds no request, permission, route or backend code
  (D5, D8).
- Good, because the story's "Given the simulated payment fails, When I click pay" maps directly to
  "choose Pago rechazado, then Pagar".
- Good, because a real gateway replaces one provider and one request type; the page's states and
  the clearing rules stay (D9).
- Bad, because a test control sits in front of every user: a real checkout never lets the buyer
  choose the outcome — mitigation: the legend says "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún
  cobro)", the confirmation repeats that no real charge was made, and the group disappears when a
  real gateway is integrated.
- Bad, because the fixed 1.5 s adds 1.5 s to every e2e payment (about 4.5 s across the planned
  runs) — mitigation: accepted; it is the time AC-15 checks and it keeps the e2e realistic.
- Bad, because quote numbers can repeat across sessions — mitigation: they are fictitious, never
  stored or looked up, and only shown once.
- Neutral: the abstract-class boundary is a small indirection for a single implementation; it is
  the seam the spec asked for (D9) and the place tests substitute.

### Strongest argument against

Option B, the mock gateway screen, is what the assessment literally names ("a confirmation screen
or a mock gateway"), and it keeps the product honest: the summary looks like a real checkout, and
the decision about the outcome is made where a real gateway would make it, on a separate screen
after "Pagar". Option A instead puts a test harness control ("Pago aprobado / Pago rechazado")
on the production summary, in front of every user, next to the button that is supposed to take
their money. An evaluator may read that as leaking test concerns into the user interface, and a
user may wonder why they are asked whether they want their payment to fail.

**Why we accept it:** B costs a new route and guard (an ADR-0001 note) or a modal dialog with its
own focus trap, splits the double-submit lock across two screens, and moves the choice after the
click, so the story's "Given … fails, When I click pay" no longer reads as written (US-03-Q-01).
Both options are equally simulated and equally deterministic; A gets there with one native radio
group, no new route and one fewer step for keyboard users. The legend and the confirmation notice
make the simulation explicit, and the gateway boundary means the control disappears with a real
integration. The human accepted this direction at HC1.

### Confirmation

- Unit: `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts` (fake timers: approved and rejected at 1500 ms, not
  at 1499 ms; in-flight rejection; abort; no HTTP), `quote-number.spec.ts` (every US-03-AC-10 row
  with a pinned `CLOCK` and a fixed `RANDOM_DIGITS`; the default source's range),
  `quote-store-clear.spec.ts` (entry and in-memory state deleted by `clearQuote()`; nothing
  removed on rejection).
- Component: `summary-page.spec.ts`: default "Pago aprobado"; exactly three form controls; three
  activations within 200 ms start one attempt (US-03-AC-09); during processing every action is
  unavailable and "Pagar" keeps focus; `aria-busy` and the status region outside it; rejection in
  `role="alert"`, state kept, focus on "Pagar"; on approval the store is cleared before the
  confirmation renders, focus and title per US-03-AC-16.
- E2E: `full-flow-co` (approved path, zero requests during payment, storage cleared, reload and
  back lead to an empty step 1, double activation) and `summary-payment-cl` (rejected, then
  approved).
- Review checklist: "Disabled pay button: its state is perceivable"; the grep and dependency checks
  above; `sessionStorage` referenced only in `QuoteStore`; no `@defer` around the confirmation.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. Visible outcome choice on the summary (chosen)

- Good, because it is deterministic for both outcomes with the same build, and discoverable by
  testers and evaluators without documentation (D2).
- Good, because it asks for no card or personal data (D1) and sends nothing (D5).
- Good, because it needs no route, guard, dialog or dependency (D8).
- Good, because the outcome is set before the click, as the story's scenario is written.
- Bad, because a simulation control is visible to every user of the production build.
- Bad, because it adds a control to the keyboard path (one more Tab stop, US-03-AC-16).

### B. Mock gateway screen

- Good, because it is the assessment's own example and mirrors a real hosted-gateway redirect.
- Good, because the summary stays free of simulation controls.
- Good, because the outcome is still deterministic and testable with the same build.
- Bad, because a route needs a guard and an ADR-0001 note (US-03-Q-06 kept the confirmation on
  `/resumen` to avoid this); a dialog needs a focus trap, `Escape` handling and focus return.
- Bad, because the double-submit lock spans "Pagar" and the gateway screen, and "cancel" on the
  gateway is a third outcome to specify.
- Bad, because the outcome is chosen after "Pagar", so AC-03, AC-04 and AC-15 would be rewritten.

### C. Deterministic rule on the input (magic values)

- Good, because there is no extra UI; real gateway sandboxes work this way.
- Good, because it is deterministic.
- Bad, because it is hidden: production code contains behaviour only testers know about, which is
  test-only logic in the shipped build.
- Bad, because it reads personal data (document number or plate) in the payment path, and the
  key may not exist: editors can remove or rename fields (US-01; ADR-0001).
- Bad, because the CL e2e must use different, "magic" step 1 data instead of the shared fictitious
  seed values; the URL-parameter variant is equally hidden and can be shared by link.

### D. Random outcome

- Good, because there is no extra UI and it feels like a real, occasionally failing gateway.
- Bad, because it is not deterministic (against BR-08): a user or a demo fails at random, and the
  e2e must patch `Math.random` or the crypto source through an init script, a test-only
  manipulation of the build.
- Bad, because a flaky outcome makes manual QA at HC3 non-repeatable.

### E. Fictitious test card form

- Good, because it looks like a real checkout and exercises form validation.
- Bad, because it invites real card entry: browsers offer to autofill saved real cards into fields
  marked as card fields, and nothing stops a person from typing their own card (against D1, the
  assessment's "do not use real card data").
- Bad, because card-shaped data would sit in the page's memory and in any error log by accident,
  which a real system would handle under PCI DSS; avoiding it entirely is simpler and safer.
- Bad, because it adds fields, validation and copy for no requirement.

## Spec impact

None that changes an AC. The approved spec v0.1 describes this option (US-03-Q-01, AC-15, §8.1).
Precisions this ADR adds, for the test-engineer and the developers:

- The spec's `payment.spec.ts` is named `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts` (§11 left the name to
  this ADR).
- "Disabled" during processing (US-03-BR-05, AC-03) is `aria-disabled="true"` on "Pagar" so it
  keeps focus (consistent with US-03-Q-17); Playwright's `toBeDisabled()` accepts `aria-disabled`
  (verified, `playwright/types/test.d.ts` 1.65.1: "Element is disabled if it has 'disabled'
  attribute or is disabled via 'aria-disabled'").
- US-03-AC-15's "1.5 seconds after the activation" is measured from the test process with a
  tolerance, because the page clock is pinned.

## More Information

- Verified on 2026-11-21 in the installed packages: `@angular/core` 22.3.0, `vitest` 5.1.1,
  `@playwright/test` and `playwright-core` 1.65.1 (versions read from each `package.json` under
  `frontend/node_modules`):
  - `page.clock.setFixedTime` keeps timers running; `page.clock.install` fakes timers until
    `runFor`/`fastForward` (`playwright-core/types/types.d.ts`, `Clock` interface).
  - `toBeDisabled()` covers `aria-disabled` (`playwright/types/test.d.ts`).
  - `vi.useFakeTimers` and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` (`vitest/dist/index.d.ts`, lines 437 and
    473).
  - `CLOCK` is `InjectionToken<() => Date>` in `frontend/src/app/core/clock.ts`.
  - The nginx allow-list (`frontend/nginx/default.conf.template`) answers `405` to any method other
    than `GET`/`HEAD`, which is why the backend mock endpoint is excluded.
- MDN, `Crypto.getRandomValues()`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Crypto/getRandomValues, read 2026-11-21):
  fills the array with cryptographically random numbers; usable from an insecure context.
- MDN, `aria-busy`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Reference/Attributes/aria-busy,
  read 2026-11-21).
- MDN, HTML `disabled` attribute
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Attributes/disabled, read
  2026-11-21): "disabled controls cannot receive focus".
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (route and guards unchanged), ADR-0002 and ADR-0005 (read-only access;
  why a backend mock is excluded), ADR-0003 (clearing rules), ADR-0007 (price shown, not passed to
  the gateway).
- Revisit when: a real payment provider is integrated (replace `SimulatedPaymentGateway`, remove
  the outcome choice, use the provider's hosted fields so card data never touches this app), or
  the product needs a stored quote or receipt (needs a server; out of scope).
