--- status: Proposed date: 2026-11-21 decision-makers: Felipe Sabogal (approval at HC2), architect subagent (proposal) consulted: specs/US-03/spec.md v0.1 (Approved; §4 BR-07, §5 AC-02, AC-12, AC-13, AC-14, AC-17, §6 US-03-Q-02, §7), specs/US-03/seed-terms.md, ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ADR-0005, ADR-0006, reviews of US-01 and US-02, `review-checklist` and `strapi-content-modeling` skills, installed packages @strapi/types, @strapi/core, @strapi/database, @strapi/utils, @strapi/content-manager 5.63.0 and @angular/core, @angular/common, @angular/platform-browser 22.3.0, npm registry (marked 18.2.1, markdown-it 15.0.3, ngx-markdown 22.1.1, @strapi/blocks-react-renderer 1.0.2, blocks-html-renderer 1.0.7), angular.dev security guide informed: all agents via CLAUDE.md precedence; future stories with editor-formatted text (help texts) --- # ADR-0009: Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings ## Context and Problem Statement The summary shows the terms and conditions of the person's country. Their text is managed by the business team in Strapi, keeps its formatting (headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic), and must be rendered "without executing anything an editor typed" (US-03-BR-07, US-03-AC-13). We must decide the Strapi attribute type of the terms `body`, the wire format the front end accepts, how it becomes DOM without an XSS path, what happens to formatting the app does not support and to malformed content, and whether a new dependency is needed. The human accepted the spec's proposal at HC1 (US-03-Q-02: "OK", Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-21) and asked for it to be weighed against real alternatives. The same choice is likely to be reused for other editor-formatted text (help texts). Story: US-03 (`specs/US-03/spec.md` §4 BR-07, §6 US-03-Q-02, §7.1, §7.2). ## Decision Drivers - D1. Editor content is never executed: no script, element or attribute an editor typed is added to the page (source: US-03-AC-13; Assessment, security; `review-checklist`: "Rich text from Strapi … is rendered safely: no `bypassSecurityTrust*`, and `[innerHTML]` only with Angular sanitisation"). - D2. Formatting is kept: headings, paragraphs, ordered and unordered lists, bold, italic (source: US-03-BR-07, US-03-AC-13 "Formatting is kept"; seed annex). - D3. "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change … from Strapi without requesting a deployment" (source: Assessment); editors use the admin, not a markup language. - D4. Editors must not be able to save something the front end cannot parse; no free JSON (source: ADR-0006; `strapi-content-modeling` skill). - D5. Malformed or unsupported content is dropped at the boundary with a warning that names the problem, never the text, and the page keeps working (source: US-01-Q-18, US-02-Q-18, spec §7.2; CLAUDE.md §3). - D6. No new dependency unless needed; every dependency is pinned exactly (source: CLAUDE.md §4). - D7. Accessibility: the terms are a named region with a correct heading hierarchy under the section heading (source: Assessment, accessibility; US-03-AC-17). - D8. Requests stay on the read-only content path; nothing else is fetched to show the terms (source: ADR-0002; US-03-AC-19). ## Considered Options 1. **A. Plain text**: `body` is a Strapi `text` attribute; the front end splits it into paragraphs on blank lines and interpolates each one. 2. **B. Markdown**: `body` is a Strapi `richtext` attribute (Markdown); a Markdown library (`marked`, `markdown-it`, or `ngx-markdown`) produces an HTML string, bound with `[innerHTML]` and cleaned by Angular's sanitiser. 3. **C. `blocks` to HTML string**: `body` is a Strapi `blocks` attribute; the front end serialises the JSON to an HTML string (own code or a library such as `blocks-html-renderer`) and binds it with `[innerHTML]` through Angular's sanitiser. 4. **D. `blocks` with a whitelist renderer**: `body` is a Strapi `blocks` attribute; a boundary parser turns the JSON into a small typed tree of supported nodes, and an Angular component renders that tree with template control flow and text interpolation only. A variant of B, parsing Markdown into tokens and rendering them through templates (no `[innerHTML]`), is folded into B's assessment: it still needs a dependency and still has to decide what to do with raw HTML inside the Markdown. ## Decision Outcome Chosen option: **"D. `blocks` with a whitelist renderer"**, because it is the only option with no HTML string anywhere in the path, so there is nothing to sanitise and nothing to bypass (D1); it keeps every formatting the spec requires (D2); editors use Strapi's visual rich-text editor and the server validates the node structure before saving (D3, D4); and it needs no new dependency (D6). Unsupported nodes degrade to text or are dropped, with a value-free warning (D5). ### What is decided **Strapi attribute (strapi-developer)** - `body`: `{ "type": "blocks", "required": true }` on the terms content type (`api::term.term`, spec §7.1, US-03-Q-03). `blocks` is a scalar attribute (`@strapi/utils@5.63.0` `dist/content-types.js:258-265`: scalar means not media, component, relation or dynamic zone), so it is selected with `fields[1]=body` and needs no `populate` (spec §7.2 request unchanged). It is stored as JSON (`@strapi/database@5.63.0` `dist/fields/index.js:33`, `blocks: json`). - Strapi validates the structure on save (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/services/entity-validator/blocks-validator.js`): root nodes must be `paragraph`, `heading` (`level` 1–6), `quote`, `code`, `list` (`format` `ordered` | `unordered`) or `image`; inline nodes `text` or `link`; link URLs limited to `http:`, `https:`, `ftp:`, `mailto:`, `tel:` (lines 18–32). `required` only rejects `null`/missing and is not applied to drafts (`dist/services/entity-validator/index.js:46-58`, 290-300): **an empty array passes**, so the front end still checks for text. - The seed (`specs/US-03/seed-terms.md`) is written in this JSON shape; for example CO block 1: `{ "type": "paragraph", "children": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Este documento es " }, { "type": "text", "text": "ficticio", "bold": true }, { "type": "text", "text": " y se usa …" } ] }`, block 3 `{ "type": "heading", "level": 2, "children": [ … ] }`, block 4 `{ "type": "list", "format": "unordered", "children": [ { "type": "list-item", "children": [ … ] }, … ] }`. **Wire type (front end, matches Strapi 5.63.0)** The front end does not depend on `@strapi/types` (that would be a new dependency, D6). It declares a wire type that mirrors `@strapi/types@5.63.0` `dist/schema/attribute/definitions/blocks.d.ts` exactly, and treats the received value as `unknown` until the parser has checked it: | Node | Shape in Strapi 5.63.0 (`blocks.d.ts`) | |---|---| | root value | `RootNode[]` | | `paragraph`, `quote` | `{ type, children: (TextInlineNode \| LinkInlineNode)[] }` | | `heading` | `{ type: 'heading', level: 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4 \| 5 \| 6, children: … }` | | `code` | `{ type: 'code', language?: string, children: … }` | | `list` | `{ type: 'list', format: 'ordered' \| 'unordered', children: (ListItemInlineNode \| ListBlockNode)[], indentLevel?: number }` (a nested list is a **sibling** of the list items) | | `list-item` | `{ type: 'list-item', children: (TextInlineNode \| LinkInlineNode)[] }` | | `image` | `{ type: 'image', image: MediaValue, children: [{ type: 'text', text: '' }] }` | | `text` | `{ type: 'text', text: string, bold?, italic?, underline?, strikethrough?, code?: boolean }` | | `link` | `{ type: 'link', url: string, rel: string, target: string, children: TextInlineNode[] }` | **Boundary parser (pure function, no Angular import)** `parseRichTextBlocks(value: unknown): RichTextBlock[] | null` in `frontend/src/app/shared/rich-text-blocks.ts` (types in `rich-text-blocks.model.ts`), used by the terms parser in `shared/terms.ts`. | [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |

| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNative` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validity.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-24 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal Forms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05); US-01-R3-F02 |

# Architecture Decision Records

Format: MADR 4 (see the `adr-madr` skill). Only a human sets an ADR to `Accepted` or `Rejected`.
Accepted ADRs are binding (`CLAUDE.md` §1, level 2) and are never rewritten; they are superseded.

## Index

| ADR | Title | Status | Date | Stories |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [0001](0001-multi-country-content-strategy.md) | Multi-country content strategy and country context (includes wizard routes and step guards) | Accepted (amended by ADR-0006) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0002](0002-strapi-access-and-security.md) | Strapi access and security model | Accepted (amended by ADR-0005) | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0003](0003-wizard-state-persistence.md) | Front-end persistence of the wizard state | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01, US-02, US-03 |
| [0004](0004-forms-library.md) | Forms library for the Strapi-driven step 1 form (Signal Forms over a shared validation core) | Accepted | 2026-11-20 | US-01 |
| [0005](0005-e2e-token-scope-for-relations.md) | Scope of the temporary e2e API token when the created content has relations (amends ADR-0002) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01 |
| [0006](0006-strapi-physical-model-adjustments.md) | Strapi physical model adjustments: typed validation-rule parameters and the country `localeTag` attribute (amends ADR-0001) | Accepted | 2026-11-21 | US-01, US-02 |
| [0007](0007-simulated-price-rule.md) | Simulated price rule: formula and factors fixed in one pure front-end function | Accepted (option A, chosen by the human at HC2, 2026-11-21) | 2026-11-21 | US-02, US-03 |
| [0008](0008-simulated-payment.md) | Simulated payment: a visible outcome choice, a front-end gateway boundary, no card data | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |
| [0009](0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md) | Terms rich text: Strapi `blocks` rendered by a whitelist component through template bindings | Proposed | 2026-11-21 | US-03 |

### Implementation notes on accepted ADRs (no decision change)

Accepted ADRs are not rewritten. When the implementation of an accepted decision changes in a way
that leaves the decision intact, the note goes here.

| ADR | Note | Since |
|---|---|---|
| 0002 | The published-only rule (ADR-0002 calls it a "global middleware") is a **route middleware** on `find`/`findOne`, attached per router through `publishedOnlyConfig()`, so that it runs after Strapi authentication. The decision (no drafts for any unauthenticated read) is unchanged. A backend test guards that every content router uses it. | c3bdb56, 345a016 (US-01-R1-F01); US-01-R2-F06 |
| 0001 | **Summary route registered by US-02 (US-02-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** The route table row `/:country/resumen` keeps its address and its kind of guard; only *who builds it, and when* moves forward. US-02 registers `/:country/resumen` with **no component** (`children: []`, the same pattern ADR-0001 used for `/:country/planes` in US-01) and a `CanActivateFn` step 3 guard, defined in US-02 spec (US-02-AC-15): no valid step 1 for the route's country → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/datos`; no chosen plan, or a stored plan key that is not an offered plan of this page load → `RedirectCommand` to `/<country>/planes`; both with `replaceUrl: true`. US-03 attaches its page to that route without changing the address or the guard, and may extend the guard only through its own spec. No new decision: ADR-0001 fixed the addresses, the per-step guards, the `RedirectCommand`/`replaceUrl` mechanics and the "earlier story registers the route, later story attaches the page" pattern; it left the guard's content to a story spec. | US-02 spec v0.1 (US-02-Q-03, US-02-AC-15) |
| 0002 | **Terms content-type name (US-03-Q-03, HC1 2026-11-21).** ADR-0002 names the US-03 permission `api::terms.terms.find`. Strapi 5.63.0 refuses a content type whose singular and plural names are equal (`@strapi/core@5.63.0` `dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`, `validateContentTypesUnicity`: "The plural name … should be unique"), so the type is **`api::term.term`** (singularName `term`, pluralName `terms`, as in CLAUDE.md §6). Consequently: the public permission is **`api::term.term.find`** (no `findOne`), reconciled in bootstrap with the existing three; the router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object (US-01-R2-F03), so `backend/tests/published-only-routes.test.ts` covers it; the REST path stays **`/api/terms`**, which must be added to the GET-only allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template` (today `countries|form-fields|plans`). The decision (public `find` only, published-only reads, GET-only proxy, no write token in the browser) is unchanged. | US-03 spec v0.1 (US-03-Q-03, §7.4) |
| 0004 | The submit gate is Signal Forms validity, as decided: `submission.action` runs only for a valid form, and `onInvalid` focuses the first invalid field in `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`. A native `number`/`date` input the browser cannot read gets a Signal Forms `parse` error, and its control model is deliberately left unwritten (writing `''` would erase the visible text). The store therefore follows the control: `syncNative` is the only writer of number and date keys (`''` on `validity.badInput`), and `flushModel()` writes the other types before `completeStep1` (keyboard Enter). 40606e2 had moved the gate to the store with `ignoreValidators: 'all'`, which broke the AC-24 keyboard submit (patched in e92e2c7) and let an emptied date through (US-01-R3-F01). The human chose to restore the Signal Forms gate in eeb23e6. | e92e2c7, eeb23e6 (US-01-R3-F01, R3-F05); US-01-R3-F02 |

input.message: I wrote both US-03 ADRs as `Proposed` and recorded the ADR-0002 implementation note. Nothing was committed, and the only changes are the four files below. Neither ADR changes an AC in the approved spec. Each adds small details, listed under "Spec impact" at the end. ## Files - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0008-simulated-payment.md` (new, Proposed) - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/0009-terms-rich-text-rendering.md` (new, Proposed) - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/adr/README.md`: index rows 0008 and 0009 as `Proposed`; the ADR-0002 implementation note; backlog text updated. - `/Users/cristiansabogal/Proyectos/multicountry-car-insurance/specs/US-03/tasks.md`: Current step `HC2`, Blockers, Next action, Last updated, T-01/T-02/T-03 set to done, and a new Gate history row. ## ADR-0008: Simulated payment **Decision (option A):** the summary shows a native radio group, "Simulación de pago (no se realiza ningún cobro)", with "Pago aprobado" (the default) and "Pago rechazado". The choice is read once when "Pagar" is activated and is kept only in the page's memory. - **Gateway boundary:** an abstract class `PaymentGateway` in `core/payment-gateway.ts`, with `pay(request, signal)`. The request carries only `simulatedOutcome`. `SimulatedPaymentGateway` has no `HttpClient`. - **Delay and clock:** the 1.5 s wait goes through an injectable `PAYMENT_DELAY`. It must be timer-based, not a loop on `Date.now()`. The quote date comes from `CLOCK`. - **Double submit, three layers:** - a synchronous page guard that sets `processing` before any `await`; - an in-flight flag in the gateway; - "Pagar" uses `aria-disabled` so it keeps focus, and every other action is locked. - **Leaving mid-payment:** the attempt is aborted when the page is destroyed, so going back during processing clears nothing. - **Quote number:** `COT---<6 digits>`, built by a pure `formatQuoteNumber` plus a `RANDOM_DIGITS` token. The default uses `crypto.getRandomValues` with rejection sampling. - **On success:** a new `QuoteStore` method (e.g. `clearQuote()`) clears the state before the confirmation is shown. On rejection nothing is cleared. - **Accessibility:** the status and alert regions sit outside the `aria-busy` subtree. - **Card data:** a reviewer can verify none exists. There are exactly three form controls, no `cc-*` autocomplete, and no new dependency. The unit test checks for HTTP calls with `HttpTestingController.verify()`, and the e2e counts zero requests during payment. A grep check is listed in the ADR. - **Options weighed:** - B: mock gateway screen; - C: magic input value, or a URL parameter; - D: random outcome; - E: fictitious test card form; - excluded: a backend mock endpoint. It contradicts ADR-0002 (GET-only proxy, `find`-only public role, and US-03-AC-19 forbids sending the plan or values). - **Strongest argument against:** option B, a mock gateway screen, is what the assessment names. Option A puts a test-harness control on the production checkout, in front of every user. We accept it because B needs a new route and guard (or a dialog with a focus trap), splits the double-submit lock across two screens, and moves the choice after the click, which breaks the story's Given/When order. The label and the confirmation notice make the simulation explicit. ## ADR-0009: Terms rich text **Decision (option D):** `body` is a Strapi `blocks` attribute, required. - **Parser:** a pure `parseRichTextBlocks()` in `shared/rich-text-blocks.ts` turns the `unknown` value into a typed whitelist tree. - Link becomes its text; quote and code blocks become paragraphs; images are dropped. - The inline `code` mark is ignored. - A nested list is attached to the preceding item, which gives valid `ul > li > ul`. - Unknown or wrong-shape nodes are dropped, with a warning that names only the type. - A body with no non-blank text makes the whole entry malformed. - **Renderer:** the `RichText` component (`app-rich-text`) uses fixed `@switch`/`@if` element names and `{{ }}` text only. There is no `[innerHTML]`, no sanitizer, no URL or attribute binding, and no new dependency. Heading levels are relative and taken from a `headingLevel` input. - **Options weighed:** - A: plain text (fails the formatting rule BR-07); - B: Markdown `richtext` with a library and sanitised `[innerHTML]`; - C: `blocks` serialised to an HTML string with `[innerHTML]`. - **Strongest argument against:** option B relies on Angular's maintained sanitizer and a mature parser. Option D puts our own parser of a Strapi-defined format on the security boundary, there is no upstream Angular renderer, the format can drift on a Strapi upgrade, and links are lost. We accept it because our code emits only typed objects, so a bug can drop text but cannot inject an element. With stock settings, B fails AC-13 as written: `marked` passes raw HTML through, and Angular's sanitizer keeps `` and `` (I verified both). ## ADR-0002 implementation note (US-03-Q-03) The type is `api::term.term` (singular `term`, plural `terms`). The permission is `api::term.term.find`, with no `findOne`. The router is `createCoreRouter('api::term.term', publishedOnlyConfig())` with a fresh config object. The path stays `/api/terms`, and it must be added to the nginx allow-list in `frontend/nginx/default.conf.template`, which today is `countries|form-fields|plans`. The decision itself is unchanged. No ADR-0001 note is needed, because Q-06 kept the confirmation on `/resumen`. ## What I verified (installed packages: Strapi 5.63.0, Angular 22.3.0) - **`blocks` shape:** the node shapes, including nested lists as siblings of list items, the optional `indentLevel`, and the `code` mark, match `@strapi/types/dist/schema/attribute/definitions/blocks.d.ts`. The frontend wire type in ADR-0009 mirrors this table. - **Server validation:** `@strapi/core/.../blocks-validator.js` checks node types and limits link protocols to http, https, ftp, mailto and tel. - **`required` lets an empty body through:** it only rejects null or missing values and is not applied to drafts (`entity-validator/index.js:46-58, 290-300`). The front end therefore still checks for non-blank text. - **Storage and selection:** `blocks` is stored as JSON and `richtext` as a string (`@strapi/database fields/index.js`). `blocks` is a scalar attribute (`@strapi/utils content-types.js:258-265`), so `fields[]=body` works without `populate`. - **Admin editor:** it offers inline code and the other modifiers (`@strapi/content-manager .../BlocksInput/Modifiers.mjs`). - **Name clash:** the plural-name uniqueness check is in `@strapi/core dist/loaders/apis.js:44-62`. - **Angular:** - The sanitizer allow-lists include `img`, `b`, `src`, `tabindex` and `role` (`@angular/core _debug_node-chunk.mjs:3164-3176`). - Text interpolation writes `nodeValue` (`platform-browser _dom_renderer-chunk.mjs:679-681`). - `NgTemplateOutlet` exists. - **Test tooling:** - Playwright 1.65.1: `setFixedTime` keeps timers running, and `toBeDisabled()` accepts `aria-disabled`. - Vitest 5.1.1 has `useFakeTimers` and `advanceTimersByTimeAsync`. - **npm and docs:** - `marked` 18.2.1 (README says it does not sanitise; checked with `npm pack`), `markdown-it` 15.0.3, `ngx-markdown` 22.1.1, `@strapi/blocks-react-renderer` 1.0.2 (React only), `blocks-html-renderer` 1.0.7. - angular.dev security page; MDN pages for `getRandomValues` (usable over plain HTTP), `aria-busy` and the `disabled` attribute. ## Spec impact (no AC changes; the spec was not edited) 1. **ADR-0008:** - The spec's `payment.spec.ts` becomes `simulated-payment-gateway.spec.ts`. - "Disabled during processing" (BR-05, AC-03) means `aria-disabled`, which is consistent with Q-17. - AC-15's "1.5 s" is measured from the test process with a tolerance, because the page clock is pinned. 2. **ADR-0009:** - The spec's phrase "one level below the section heading" is ambiguous. I read it as below the terms title: `h4` if the title is `h3` under the `h2` "Términos y condiciones". The spec or the developer still has to fix which element the title uses. - The parser lives in `shared/rich-text-blocks.ts`. - The spec does not mention the inline `code` mark or nested lists; the ADR covers both. - The seed in `seed-terms.md` must be written in the `blocks` JSON shape; the ADR gives an example. ## Not verified - I only partly checked that `markdown-it`'s *default* preset sets `html: false`: grep found two `html: false` and two `html: true` occurrences in the dist file, and I did not map them to presets. - Whether the Strapi admin can hide blocks toolbar buttons per field. The ADR avoids relying on it. - That a native `button` turns Enter and Space into one `click` (standard HTML, not checked against a source). - How screen readers actually announce the processing state. That is left to the HC3 screen-reader pass.
